segs.e: Numbered Discourses 3.1
1. Fools
Perils
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Yāni kānici, bhikkhave, bhayāni uppajjanti sabbāni tāni bālato uppajjanti, no paṇḍitato.
segs.e: “Whatever dangers there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

segs.p: Ye keci upaddavā uppajjanti sabbe te bālato uppajjanti, no paṇḍitato.
segs.e: Whatever perils there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

segs.p: Ye keci upasaggā uppajjanti sabbe te bālato uppajjanti, no paṇḍitato.
segs.e: Whatever hazards there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, naḷāgārā vā tiṇāgārā vā aggi mutto kūṭāgārānipi ḍahati ullittāvalittāni nivātāni phusitaggaḷāni pihitavātapānāni;
segs.e: It’s like a fire that spreads from a hut made of reeds or grass, and burns down even a bungalow, plastered inside and out, draft-free, with doors fastened and windows shuttered.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yāni kānici bhayāni uppajjanti sabbāni tāni bālato uppajjanti, no paṇḍitato.
segs.e: In the same way, whatever dangers there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

segs.p: Ye keci upaddavā uppajjanti sabbe te bālato uppajjanti, no paṇḍitato.
segs.e: Whatever perils there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

segs.p: Ye keci upasaggā uppajjanti sabbe te bālato uppajjanti, no paṇḍitato.
segs.e: Whatever hazards there are, all come from the foolish, not from the astute.

segs.p: Iti kho, bhikkhave, sappaṭibhayo bālo, appaṭibhayo paṇḍito.
segs.e: So, the fool is dangerous, but the astute person is safe.
The fool is perilous, but the astute person is not.
The fool is hazardous, but the astute person is not.

segs.p: Natthi, bhikkhave, paṇḍitato bhayaṁ, natthi paṇḍitato upaddavo, natthi paṇḍitato upasaggo.
segs.e: There’s no danger, peril, or hazard that comes from the astute.
So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘yehi tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo te tayo dhamme abhinivajjetvā, yehi tīhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo te tayo dhamme samādāya vattissāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will shun the three things by which a fool is known, and we will proceed having undertaken the three things by which an astute person is known.’
That’s how you should train.”
Numbered Discourses 3.2
1. Fools
Characteristics

segs.p: “Kammalakkhaṇo, bhikkhave, bālo, kammalakkhaṇo paṇḍito, apadānasobhanī paññāti.
segs.e: “A fool is characterized by their deeds, and an astute person is characterized by their deeds, for wisdom shines in its traces.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo.
segs.e: A fool is known by three things.
What three?
Bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo.
segs.e: These are the three things by which a fool is known.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo.
segs.e: An astute person is known by three things.
What three?
Good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo.
segs.e: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.
So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘yehi tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo te tayo dhamme abhinivajjetvā, yehi tīhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo te tayo dhamme samādāya vattissāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will shun the three things by which a fool is known, and we will proceed having undertaken the three things by which an astute person is known.’
That’s how you should train.”
Numbered Discourses 3.3
1. Fools
Thinking
“There are these three characteristics, signs, and manifestations of a fool.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bālo duccintitacintī ca hoti dubbhāsitabhāsī ca dukkaṭakammakārī ca.
segs.e: A fool thinks poorly, speaks poorly, and acts poorly.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, bālo duccintitacintī ca abhavissa dubbhāsitabhāsī ca dukkaṭakammakārī ca, kena naṁ paṇḍitā jāneyyuṁ:
segs.e: If a fool didn’t think poorly, speak poorly, and act poorly, then how would the astute know of them:
‘This worthy one is a fool, an untrue person’?

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, bālo duccintitacintī ca hoti dubbhāsitabhāsī ca dukkaṭakammakārī ca tasmā naṁ paṇḍitā jānanti:
segs.e: But since a fool does think poorly, speak poorly, and act poorly, then the astute do know of them:
‘This worthy one is a fool, an untrue person’.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi bālassa bālalakkhaṇāni bālanimittāni bālāpadānāni.
segs.e: These are the three characteristics, signs, and manifestations of a fool.

segs.p: Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, paṇḍitassa paṇḍitalakkhaṇāni paṇḍitanimittāni paṇḍitāpadānāni.
segs.e: There are these three characteristics, signs, and manifestations of an astute person.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, paṇḍito sucintitacintī ca hoti subhāsitabhāsī ca sukatakammakārī ca.
segs.e: An astute person thinks well, speaks well, and acts well.

segs.p: No cedaṁ, bhikkhave, paṇḍito sucintitacintī ca abhavissa subhāsitabhāsī ca sukatakammakārī ca, kena naṁ paṇḍitā jāneyyuṁ:
segs.e: If an astute person didn’t think well, speak well, and act well, then how would the astute know of them:
‘This worthy one is astute, a true person’?

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, paṇḍito sucintitacintī ca hoti subhāsitabhāsī ca sukatakammakārī ca tasmā naṁ paṇḍitā jānanti:
segs.e: But since an astute person does think well, speak well, and act well, then the astute do know of them:
‘This worthy one is astute, a true person’.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi paṇḍitassa paṇḍitalakkhaṇāni paṇḍitanimittāni paṇḍitāpadānāni.
segs.e: These are the three characteristics, signs, and manifestations of an astute person.
So you should train …”
Numbered Discourses 3.4
1. Fools
Mistakes
“A fool is known by three things.
What three?

segs.p: Accayaṁ accayato na passati, accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ nappaṭikaroti, parassa kho pana accayaṁ desentassa yathādhammaṁ nappaṭiggaṇhāti.
segs.e: They don’t recognize when they’ve made a mistake. When they do recognize it they don’t deal with it properly. And when someone else confesses a mistake to them, they don’t accept it properly.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo.
segs.e: These are the three things by which a fool is known.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo.
segs.e: An astute person is known by three things.
What three?

segs.p: Accayaṁ accayato passati, accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ paṭikaroti, parassa kho pana accayaṁ desentassa yathādhammaṁ paṭiggaṇhāti.
segs.e: They recognize when they’ve made a mistake. When they recognize it they deal with it properly. And when someone else confesses a mistake to them, they accept it properly.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo.
segs.e: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.
So you should train …”
Numbered Discourses 3.5
1. Fools
Irrational
“A fool is known by three things.
What three?

segs.p: Ayoniso pañhaṁ kattā hoti, ayoniso pañhaṁ vissajjetā hoti, parassa kho pana yoniso pañhaṁ vissajjitaṁ parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi siliṭṭhehi upagatehi nābbhanumoditā hoti.
segs.e: They ask a question irrationally. They answer a question irrationally. And when someone else answers a question rationally—with well-rounded, coherent, and relevant words and phrases—they disagree with it.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo.
segs.e: These are the three things by which a fool is known.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo.
segs.e: An astute person is known by three things.
What three?

segs.p: Yoniso pañhaṁ kattā hoti, yoniso pañhaṁ vissajjetā hoti, parassa kho pana yoniso pañhaṁ vissajjitaṁ parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi siliṭṭhehi upagatehi abbhanumoditā hoti.
segs.e: They ask a question rationally. They answer a question rationally. And when someone else answers a question rationally—with well-rounded, coherent, and relevant words and phrases—they agree with it.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo.
segs.e: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.
So you should train …”
Numbered Discourses 3.6
1. Fools
Unskillful
“A fool is known by three things.
What three?

segs.p: Akusalena kāyakammena, akusalena vacīkammena, akusalena manokammena.
segs.e: Unskillful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo.
segs.e: These are the three things by which a fool is known.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo.
segs.e: An astute person is known by three things.
What three?

segs.p: Kusalena kāyakammena, kusalena vacīkammena, kusalena manokammena.
segs.e: Skillful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo.
segs.e: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.
So you should train …”
Numbered Discourses 3.7
1. Fools
Blameworthy
“A fool is known by three things.
What three?

segs.p: Sāvajjena kāyakammena, sāvajjena vacīkammena, sāvajjena manokammena …pe… anavajjena kāyakammena, anavajjena vacīkammena, anavajjena manokammena …pe….
segs.e: Blameworthy deeds by way of body, speech, and mind. … An astute person is known by blameless deeds by way of body, speech, and mind. …”
Numbered Discourses 3.8
1. Fools
Hurtful
“A fool is known by three things.
What three?

segs.p: Sabyābajjhena kāyakammena, sabyābajjhena vacīkammena, sabyābajjhena manokammena …pe… abyābajjhena kāyakammena, abyābajjhena vacīkammena, abyābajjhena manokammena.
segs.e: Hurtful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind. … An astute person is known by kind deeds by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Imehi, kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo.
segs.e: These are the three things by which an astute person is known.
So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘yehi tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo te tayo dhamme abhinivajjetvā, yehi tīhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo te tayo dhamme samādāya vattissāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will shun the three qualities by which a fool is known, and we will proceed having undertaken the three qualities by which an astute person is known.’
That’s how you should train.”
Numbered Discourses 3.9
1. Fools
Broken

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bālo abyatto asappuriso khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo ca viññūnaṁ, bahuñca apuññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: “When a foolish, incompetent, untrue person has three qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.
What three?
Bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo abyatto asappuriso khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo ca viññūnaṁ, bahuñca apuññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: When a foolish, incompetent untrue person possesses these three qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito viyatto sappuriso akkhataṁ anupahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, anavajjo ca hoti ananuvajjo ca viññūnaṁ, bahuñca puññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: When an astute, competent true person has three qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.
What three?
Good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito viyatto sappuriso akkhataṁ anupahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, anavajjo ca hoti ananuvajjo ca viññūnaṁ, bahuñca puññaṁ pasavatī”ti.
segs.e: When an astute, competent true person possesses these three qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.”
Numbered Discourses 3.10
1. Fools
Stains

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato tayo male appahāya yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Anyone who has three qualities, and has not given up three stains, is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What three?

segs.p: Dussīlo ca hoti, dussīlyamalañcassa appahīnaṁ hoti;
segs.e: They’re unethical, and haven’t given up the stain of immorality.

segs.p: issukī ca hoti, issāmalañcassa appahīnaṁ hoti;
segs.e: They’re jealous, and haven’t given up the stain of jealousy.

segs.p: maccharī ca hoti, maccheramalañcassa appahīnaṁ hoti.
segs.e: They’re stingy, and haven’t given up the stain of stinginess.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato ime tayo male appahāya yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Anyone who possesses these three qualities, and has not given up these three stains, is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato tayo male pahāya yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Anyone who has three qualities, and has given up three stains, is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What three?

segs.p: Sīlavā ca hoti, dussīlyamalañcassa pahīnaṁ hoti;
segs.e: They’re ethical, and have given up the stain of immorality.

segs.p: anissukī ca hoti, issāmalañcassa pahīnaṁ hoti;
segs.e: They’re not jealous, and have given up the stain of jealousy.

segs.p: amaccharī ca hoti, maccheramalañcassa pahīnaṁ hoti.
segs.e: They’re not stingy, and have given up the stain of stinginess.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato ime tayo male pahāya yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Anyone who possesses these three qualities, and has given up these three stains, is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 3.11
2. The Chariot-Maker
Well-known

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ñāto bhikkhu bahujanaahitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanadukkhāya, bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a well-known mendicant with three qualities is acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.
What three?

segs.p: Ananulomike kāyakamme samādapeti, ananulomike vacīkamme samādapeti, ananulomikesu dhammesu samādapeti.
segs.e: They encourage deeds of body and speech, as well as principles, that aren’t in line with good qualities.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato ñāto bhikkhu bahujanaahitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanadukkhāya, bahuno janassa anatthāya ahitāya dukkhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: A well-known mendicant who possesses these three qualities is acting for the detriment and unhappiness of the people, against the people, for the harm, detriment, and suffering of gods and humans.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ñāto bhikkhu bahujanahitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: A well-known mendicant with three qualities is acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
What three?

segs.p: Anulomike kāyakamme samādapeti, anulomike vacīkamme samādapeti, anulomikesu dhammesu samādapeti.
segs.e: They encourage deeds of body and speech, as well as principles, that are in line with good qualities.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato ñāto bhikkhu bahujanahitāya paṭipanno hoti bahujanasukhāya, bahuno janassa atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: A well-known mendicant who possesses these three qualities is acting for the welfare and happiness of the people, for the people, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.”
Numbered Discourses 3.12
2. The Chariot-Maker
Commemoration

segs.p: “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyāni bhavanti.
segs.e: “An anointed aristocratic king should commemorate three places as long as he lives.
What three?

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, padese rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto jāto hoti.
segs.e: The place he was born.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṁ rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the first place.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ padese rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto hoti.
segs.e: The place he was anointed as king.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṁ rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the second place.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ padese rājā khattiyo muddhāvasitto saṅgāmaṁ abhivijinitvā vijitasaṅgāmo tameva saṅgāmasīsaṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: The place where he won victory in battle, establishing himself as foremost in battle.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṁ rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the third place.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyāni bhavanti.
segs.e: These are the three places an anointed king should commemorate as long as he lives.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tīṇimāni bhikkhussa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyāni bhavanti.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant should commemorate three places as long as they live.
What three?

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, padese bhikkhu kesamassuṁ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti.
segs.e: The place where the mendicant shaved off their hair and beard, dressed in ocher robes, and went forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamaṁ bhikkhussa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the first place.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ padese bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: The place where the mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyaṁ bhikkhussa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the second place.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yasmiṁ padese bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: The place where the mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyaṁ bhikkhussa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ hoti.
segs.e: This is the third place.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi bhikkhussa yāvajīvaṁ sāraṇīyāni bhavantī”ti.
segs.e: These are the three places a mendicant should commemorate as long as they live.”
Numbered Discourses 3.13
2. The Chariot-Maker
Hopes
“These three individuals are found in the world.
What three?
The hopeless, the hopeful, and the one who has done away with hope.
And what, mendicants, is a hopeless individual?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo nīce kule paccājāto hoti, caṇḍālakule vā venakule vā nesādakule vā rathakārakule vā pukkusakule vā dalidde appannapānabhojane kasiravuttike, yattha kasirena ghāsacchādo labbhati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is reborn in a low family—a family of corpse-workers, bamboo-workers, hunters, chariot-makers, or scavengers—poor, with little to eat or drink, where life is tough, and food and shelter are hard to find.

segs.p: So ca hoti dubbaṇṇo duddasiko okoṭimako bavhābādho kāṇo vā kuṇī vā khañjo vā pakkhahato vā, na lābhī annassa pānassa vatthassa yānassa mālāgandhavilepanassa seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
segs.e: And they’re ugly, unsightly, deformed, sickly—one-eyed, crippled, lame, or half-paralyzed. They don’t get to have food, drink, clothes, and vehicles; garlands, fragrances, and makeup; or bed, house, and lighting.
They hear this:
‘They say the aristocrats have anointed the aristocrat named so-and-so as king.’
It never occurs to them:
‘Oh, when will the aristocrats anoint me too as king?’
This is called a hopeless individual.
And what, mendicants, is a hopeful individual?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa jeṭṭho putto hoti ābhiseko anabhisitto acalappatto.
segs.e: It’s when someone is the eldest son of an anointed aristocratic king. He has not yet been anointed, but is eligible, and has been confirmed in the succession.
He hears this:
‘They say that the aristocrats have anointed the aristocrat named so-and-so as king.’
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, when will the aristocrats anoint me too as king?’
This is called a hopeful individual.
And what, mendicants, is an individual who has done away with hope?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rājā hoti khattiyo muddhāvasitto.
segs.e: It’s when a king has been anointed.
He hears this:
‘They say that the aristocrats have anointed the aristocrat named so-and-so as king.’
It never occurs to him:
‘Oh, when will the aristocrats anoint me too as king?’
Why is that?

segs.p: Yā hissa, bhikkhave, pubbe anabhisittassa abhisekāsā sā paṭippassaddhā.
segs.e: Because the former hope he had to be anointed has now died down.
This is called an individual who has done away with hope.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā bhikkhūsu.
segs.e: In the same way, these three individuals are found among the mendicants.
What three?
The hopeless, the hopeful, and the one who has done away with hope.
And what, mendicants, is a hopeless individual?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dussīlo hoti pāpadhammo asuci saṅkassarasamācāro paṭicchannakammanto assamaṇo samaṇapaṭiñño abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño antopūti avassuto kasambujāto.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad qualities, filthy, with suspicious behavior, underhand, no true ascetic or spiritual practitioner—though claiming to be one—rotten inside, festering, and depraved.
They hear this:

segs.p: ‘itthannāmo kira bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘They say that the mendicant named so-and-so has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’
It never occurs to them:

segs.p: ‘kudāssu nāma ahampi āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, when will I too realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’
This is called a hopeless individual.
And what, mendicants, is a hopeful individual?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti kalyāṇadhammo.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, of good character.
They hear this:

segs.p: ‘itthannāmo kira bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘They say that the mendicant named so-and-so has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’
It occurs to them:

segs.p: ‘kudāssu nāma ahampi āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, when will I too realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’
This is called a hopeful individual.
And what, mendicants, is an individual who has done away with hope?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṁ hoti khīṇāsavo.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is a perfected one, who has ended all defilements.
They hear this:

segs.p: ‘itthannāmo kira bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘They say that the mendicant named so-and-so has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’
It never occurs to them:

segs.p: ‘kudāssu nāma ahampi āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, when will I too realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with my own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’
Why is that?

segs.p: Yā hissa, bhikkhave, pubbe avimuttassa vimuttāsā sā paṭippassaddhā.
segs.e: Because the former hope they had to be freed has now died down.
This is called an individual who has done away with hope.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā bhikkhūsū”ti.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found among the mendicants.”
Numbered Discourses 3.14
2. The Chariot-Maker
The Wheel-Turning Monarch

segs.p: “Yopi so, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā sopi na arājakaṁ cakkaṁ vattetī”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, even a wheel-turning monarch, a just and principled king, does not wield power without having their own king.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “ko pana, bhante, rañño cakkavattissa dhammikassa dhammarañño rājā”ti?
segs.e: “But who is the king of the wheel-turning monarch, the just and principled king?”
“It is principle, monk,” said the Buddha.

segs.p: “idha, bhikkhu, rājā cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaṁyeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahati antojanasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Monk, a wheel-turning monarch provides just protection and security for his court, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, rājā cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaṁyeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahati khattiyesu, anuyantesu, balakāyasmiṁ, brāhmaṇagahapatikesu, negamajānapadesu, samaṇabrāhmaṇesu, migapakkhīsu.
segs.e: He provides just protection and security for his aristocrats, vassals, troops, brahmins and householders, people of town and country, ascetics and brahmins, beasts and birds.

segs.p: Sa kho so bhikkhu rājā cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaṁyeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā antojanasmiṁ, dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā khattiyesu …pe… anuyantesu, balakāyasmiṁ, brāhmaṇagahapatikesu, negamajānapadesu, samaṇabrāhmaṇesu, migapakkhīsu, dhammeneva cakkaṁ vatteti.
segs.e: When he has done this, he wields power only in a principled manner.

segs.p: Taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ kenaci manussabhūtena paccatthikena pāṇinā.
segs.e: And this power cannot be undermined by any human enemy.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhu, tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaṁyeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahati kāyakammasmiṁ:
segs.e: In the same way, monk, a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, a just and principled king, provides just protection and security regarding bodily actions, relying only on principle—honoring, respecting, and venerating principle, having principle as his flag, banner, and authority.

segs.p: ‘evarūpaṁ kāyakammaṁ sevitabbaṁ, evarūpaṁ kāyakammaṁ na sevitabban’ti.
segs.e: ‘This kind of bodily action should be cultivated. This kind of bodily action should not be cultivated.’

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhu, tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaṁyeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahati vacīkammasmiṁ:
segs.e: Furthermore, a Realized One … provides just protection and security regarding verbal actions, saying:

segs.p: ‘evarūpaṁ vacīkammaṁ sevitabbaṁ, evarūpaṁ vacīkammaṁ na sevitabban’ti …pe… manokammasmiṁ:
segs.e: ‘This kind of verbal action should be cultivated. This kind of verbal action should not be cultivated.’ … And regarding mental actions:

segs.p: ‘evarūpaṁ manokammaṁ sevitabbaṁ, evarūpaṁ manokammaṁ na sevitabban’ti.
segs.e: ‘This kind of mental action should be cultivated. This kind of mental action should not be cultivated.’

segs.p: Sa kho so, bhikkhu, tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho dhammiko dhammarājā dhammaṁyeva nissāya dhammaṁ sakkaronto dhammaṁ garuṁ karonto dhammaṁ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā kāyakammasmiṁ, dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā vacīkammasmiṁ, dhammikaṁ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṁ saṁvidahitvā manokammasmiṁ, dhammeneva anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavatteti.
segs.e: And when a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha has provided just protection and security regarding actions of body, speech, and mind, he rolls forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma.

segs.p: Taṁ hoti cakkaṁ appaṭivattiyaṁ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: And that wheel cannot be rolled back by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or divinity or by anyone in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 3.15
2. The Chariot-Maker
About Pacetana

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ viharati isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Once upon a time, there was a king named Pacetana.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā sacetano rathakāraṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then King Pacetana addressed his chariot-maker,

segs.p: ‘ito me, samma rathakāra, channaṁ māsānaṁ accayena saṅgāmo bhavissati.
segs.e: ‘In six months’ time, my good chariot-maker, there will be a battle.

segs.p: Sakkhissasi me, samma rathakāra, navaṁ cakkayugaṁ kātun’ti?
segs.e: Are you able to make me a new pair of wheels?’

segs.p: ‘Sakkomi, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, rathakāro rañño sacetanassa paccassosi.
segs.e: ‘I can, Your Majesty,’ replied the chariot-maker.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, rathakāro chahi māsehi chārattūnehi ekaṁ cakkaṁ niṭṭhāpesi.
segs.e: Then, when it was six days less than six months later, the chariot-maker had finished one wheel.

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā sacetano rathakāraṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then King Pacetana addressed his chariot-maker,

segs.p: ‘ito me, samma rathakāra, channaṁ divasānaṁ accayena saṅgāmo bhavissati, niṭṭhitaṁ navaṁ cakkayugan’ti?
segs.e: ‘In six days’ time there will be a battle. Is my new pair of wheels finished?’

segs.p: ‘Imehi kho, deva, chahi māsehi chārattūnehi ekaṁ cakkaṁ niṭṭhitan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Now that it is six days less than six months, Your Majesty, I have finished one wheel.’

segs.p: ‘Sakkhissasi pana me, samma rathakāra, imehi chahi divasehi dutiyaṁ cakkaṁ niṭṭhāpetun’ti?
segs.e: ‘Are you able to finish the second wheel in these six days?’

segs.p: ‘Sakkomi, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, rathakāro chahi divasehi dutiyaṁ cakkaṁ niṭṭhāpetvā navaṁ cakkayugaṁ ādāya yena rājā sacetano tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṁ sacetanaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Saying, ‘I can, Your Majesty,’ the chariot-maker finished the second wheel in six days. Taking the pair of wheels he went up to King Pacetana, and said this to the king,
‘Your Majesty, these are your two new wheels, finished.’

segs.p: ‘Yañca te idaṁ, samma rathakāra, cakkaṁ chahi māsehi niṭṭhitaṁ chārattūnehi yañca te idaṁ cakkaṁ chahi divasehi niṭṭhitaṁ, imesaṁ kiṁ nānākaraṇaṁ?
segs.e: ‘But, my good chariot-maker, what is the difference between the wheel that was finished in six days less than six months, and the wheel finished in just six days?
Because I can’t see any difference between them.’
‘But, Your Majesty, there is a difference.
See now what it is.’

segs.p: Atha kho, bhikkhave, rathakāro yaṁ taṁ cakkaṁ chahi divasehi niṭṭhitaṁ taṁ pavattesi.
segs.e: Then the chariot-maker rolled forth the wheel that had been finished in six days.

segs.p: Taṁ pavattitaṁ samānaṁ yāvatikā abhisaṅkhārassa gati tāvatikaṁ gantvā ciṅgulāyitvā bhūmiyaṁ papati.
segs.e: It rolled as far as the original impetus took it, then wobbled and fell down.

segs.p: Yaṁ pana taṁ cakkaṁ chahi māsehi niṭṭhitaṁ chārattūnehi taṁ pavattesi.
segs.e: Then he rolled forth the wheel that had been finished in six days less than six months.

segs.p: Taṁ pavattitaṁ samānaṁ yāvatikā abhisaṅkhārassa gati tāvatikaṁ gantvā akkhāhataṁ maññe aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: It rolled as far as the original impetus took it, then stood still as if fixed to an axle.

segs.p: ‘Ko nu kho, samma rathakāra, hetu ko paccayo yamidaṁ cakkaṁ chahi divasehi niṭṭhitaṁ taṁ pavattitaṁ samānaṁ yāvatikā abhisaṅkhārassa gati tāvatikaṁ gantvā ciṅgulāyitvā bhūmiyaṁ papati?
segs.e: ‘But what is the cause, my good chariot-maker, what is the reason why the wheel that was finished in six days wobbled and fell,

segs.p: Ko pana, samma rathakāra, hetu ko paccayo yamidaṁ cakkaṁ chahi māsehi niṭṭhitaṁ chārattūnehi taṁ pavattitaṁ samānaṁ yāvatikā abhisaṅkhārassa gati tāvatikaṁ gantvā akkhāhataṁ maññe aṭṭhāsī’ti?
segs.e: while the one that was finished in six days less than six months stood still as if fixed to an axle?’

segs.p: ‘Yamidaṁ, deva, cakkaṁ chahi divasehi niṭṭhitaṁ tassa nemipi savaṅkā sadosā sakasāvā, arāpi savaṅkā sadosā sakasāvā, nābhipi savaṅkā sadosā sakasāvā.
segs.e: ‘The wheel that was finished in six days, Your Majesty, is crooked, flawed, and defective in rim, spoke, and hub.

segs.p: Taṁ nemiyāpi savaṅkattā sadosattā sakasāvattā, arānampi savaṅkattā sadosattā sakasāvattā, nābhiyāpi savaṅkattā sadosattā sakasāvattā pavattitaṁ samānaṁ yāvatikā abhisaṅkhārassa gati tāvatikaṁ gantvā ciṅgulāyitvā bhūmiyaṁ papati.
segs.e: That’s why it wobbled and fell.

segs.p: Yaṁ pana taṁ, deva, cakkaṁ chahi māsehi niṭṭhitaṁ chārattūnehi tassa nemipi avaṅkā adosā akasāvā, arāpi avaṅkā adosā akasāvā, nābhipi avaṅkā adosā akasāvā.
segs.e: The wheel that was finished in six days less than six months, Your Majesty, is not crooked, flawed, and defective in rim, spoke, and hub.

segs.p: Taṁ nemiyāpi avaṅkattā adosattā akasāvattā, arānampi avaṅkattā adosattā akasāvattā, nābhiyāpi avaṅkattā adosattā akasāvattā pavattitaṁ samānaṁ yāvatikā abhisaṅkhārassa gati tāvatikaṁ gantvā akkhāhataṁ maññe aṭṭhāsī’ti.
segs.e: That’s why it stood still as if fixed to an axle.’

segs.p: Siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, tumhākaṁ evamassa:
segs.e: Now, mendicants, you might think:

segs.p: ‘añño nūna tena samayena so rathakāro ahosī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Surely that chariot-maker must have been someone else at that time?’

segs.p: Na kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: But you should not see it like that.

segs.p: Ahaṁ tena samayena so rathakāro ahosiṁ.
segs.e: I myself was the chariot-maker at that time.

segs.p: Tadāhaṁ, bhikkhave, kusalo dāruvaṅkānaṁ dārudosānaṁ dārukasāvānaṁ.
segs.e: Then I was skilled in the crooks, flaws, and defects of wood.

segs.p: Etarahi kho panāhaṁ, bhikkhave, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho kusalo kāyavaṅkānaṁ kāyadosānaṁ kāyakasāvānaṁ, kusalo vacīvaṅkānaṁ vacīdosānaṁ vacīkasāvānaṁ, kusalo manovaṅkānaṁ manodosānaṁ manokasāvānaṁ.
segs.e: Now that I am a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, I am skilled in the crooks, flaws, and defects of actions by body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā kāyavaṅko appahīno kāyadoso kāyakasāvo, vacīvaṅko appahīno vacīdoso vacīkasāvo, manovaṅko appahīno manodoso manokasāvo, evaṁ papatitā te, bhikkhave, imasmā dhammavinayā, seyyathāpi taṁ cakkaṁ chahi divasehi niṭṭhitaṁ.
segs.e: Whatever monk or nun has not given up the crooks, flaws, and defects of body, speech, and mind has fallen from the teaching and training, just like the wheel that was finished in six days.

segs.p: Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā kāyavaṅko pahīno kāyadoso kāyakasāvo, vacīvaṅko pahīno vacīdoso vacīkasāvo, manovaṅko pahīno manodoso manokasāvo, evaṁ patiṭṭhitā te, bhikkhave, imasmiṁ dhammavinaye, seyyathāpi taṁ cakkaṁ chahi māsehi niṭṭhitaṁ chārattūnehi.
segs.e: Whatever monk or nun has given up the crooks, flaws, and defects of body, speech, and mind is established in the teaching and training, just like the wheel that was finished in six days less than six months.
So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘kāyavaṅkaṁ pajahissāma kāyadosaṁ kāyakasāvaṁ, vacīvaṅkaṁ pajahissāma vacīdosaṁ vacīkasāvaṁ, manovaṅkaṁ pajahissāma manodosaṁ manokasāvan’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will give up the crooks, flaws, and defects of body, speech, and mind.’
That’s how you should train.”
Numbered Discourses 3.16
2. The Chariot-Maker
A Sure Bet

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu apaṇṇakapaṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has three things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu indriyesu guttadvāro hoti, bhojane mattaññū hoti, jāgariyaṁ anuyutto hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant guards the sense doors, eats in moderation, and is dedicated to wakefulness.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu indriyesu guttadvāro hoti?
segs.e: And how does a mendicant guard the sense doors?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati cakkhundriyaṁ, cakkhundriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.
When they hear a sound with their ears …
When they smell an odor with their nose …
When they taste a flavor with their tongue …
When they feel a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī.
segs.e: When they know an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: Yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati, rakkhati manindriyaṁ, manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu indriyesu guttadvāro hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant guards the sense doors.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhojane mattaññū hoti?
segs.e: And how does a mendicant eat in moderation?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso āhāraṁ āhāreti:
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant reflects rationally on the food that they eat:

segs.p: ‘neva davāya na madāya na maṇḍanāya na vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya vihiṁsūparatiyā brahmacariyānuggahāya, iti purāṇañca vedanaṁ paṭihaṅkhāmi, navañca vedanaṁ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro cā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Not for fun, indulgence, adornment, or decoration, but only to sustain this body, to avoid harm, and to support spiritual practice. In this way, I shall put an end to old discomfort and not give rise to new discomfort, and I will have the means to keep going, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bhojane mattaññū hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant eats in moderation.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu jāgariyaṁ anuyutto hoti?
segs.e: And how is a mendicant dedicated to wakefulness?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu divasaṁ caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṁ parisodheti, rattiyā paṭhamaṁ yāmaṁ caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṁ parisodheti, rattiyā majjhimaṁ yāmaṁ dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṁ kappeti pāde pādaṁ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṁ manasi karitvā, rattiyā pacchimaṁ yāmaṁ paccuṭṭhāya caṅkamena nisajjāya āvaraṇīyehi dhammehi cittaṁ parisodheti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant practices walking and sitting meditation by day, purifying their mind from obstacles. In the first watch of the night, they continue to practice walking and sitting meditation. In the middle watch, they lie down in the lion’s posture—on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other—mindful and aware, and focused on the time of getting up. In the last watch, they get up and continue to practice walking and sitting meditation, purifying their mind from obstacles.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu jāgariyaṁ anuyutto hoti.
segs.e: This is how a mendicant is dedicated to wakefulness.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu apaṇṇakapaṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāyā”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these three things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.”
Numbered Discourses 3.17
2. The Chariot-Maker
Hurting Yourself

segs.p: “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā attabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti, parabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “These three things, mendicants, lead to hurting yourself, hurting others, and hurting both.
What three?
Bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā attabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti, parabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These are three things that lead to hurting yourself, hurting others, and hurting both.

segs.p: Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā nevattabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti, na parabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These three things, mendicants, don’t lead to hurting yourself, hurting others, or hurting both.
What three?
Good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā nevattabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti, na parabyābādhāyapi saṁvattanti, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These are three things that don’t lead to hurting yourself, hurting others, or hurting both.”
Numbered Discourses 3.18
2. The Chariot-Maker
The Realm of the Gods

segs.p: “Sace vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṁ puccheyyuṁ:
segs.e: “Mendicants, if wanderers who follow another religion were to ask you:
‘Reverend, do you lead the spiritual life with the ascetic Gotama so that you can be reborn in the realm of the gods?’

segs.p: Nanu tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṁ puṭṭhā aṭṭīyeyyātha harāyeyyātha jiguccheyyāthā”ti?
segs.e: Being questioned like this, wouldn’t you be horrified, repelled, and disgusted?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Iti kira tumhe, bhikkhave, dibbena āyunā aṭṭīyatha harāyatha jigucchatha, dibbena vaṇṇena dibbena sukhena dibbena yasena dibbenādhipateyyena aṭṭīyatha harāyatha jigucchatha;
segs.e: “So it seems that you are horrified, repelled, and disgusted by heavenly lifespan, beauty, happiness, glory, and sovereignty.

segs.p: pageva kho pana, bhikkhave, tumhehi kāyaduccaritena aṭṭīyitabbaṁ harāyitabbaṁ jigucchitabbaṁ, vacīduccaritena … manoduccaritena aṭṭīyitabbaṁ harāyitabbaṁ jigucchitabban”ti.
segs.e: How much more then should you be horrified, embarrassed, and disgusted by bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.”
Numbered Discourses 3.19
2. The Chariot-Maker
A Shopkeeper (1st)

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato pāpaṇiko abhabbo anadhigataṁ vā bhogaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā bhogaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a shopkeeper who has three factors is unable to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpaṇiko pubbaṇhasamayaṁ na sakkaccaṁ kammantaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, majjhanhikasamayaṁ na sakkaccaṁ kammantaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, sāyanhasamayaṁ na sakkaccaṁ kammantaṁ adhiṭṭhāti.
segs.e: It’s when a shopkeeper doesn’t carefully focus on their work in the morning, at midday, and in the afternoon.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi aṅgehi samannāgato pāpaṇiko abhabbo anadhigataṁ vā bhogaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā bhogaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: A shopkeeper who has these three factors is unable to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo anadhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with three qualities is unable to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pubbaṇhasamayaṁ na sakkaccaṁ samādhinimittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, majjhanhikasamayaṁ na sakkaccaṁ samādhinimittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, sāyanhasamayaṁ na sakkaccaṁ samādhinimittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t carefully focus on a meditation subject as a basis of immersion in the morning, at midday, and in the afternoon.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu abhabbo anadhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these three qualities is unable to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.

segs.p: Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato pāpaṇiko bhabbo anadhigataṁ vā bhogaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā bhogaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: A shopkeeper who has three factors is able to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpaṇiko pubbaṇhasamayaṁ sakkaccaṁ kammantaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, majjhanhikasamayaṁ …pe… sāyanhasamayaṁ sakkaccaṁ kammantaṁ adhiṭṭhāti.
segs.e: It’s when a shopkeeper carefully focuses on their work in the morning, at midday, and in the afternoon.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi aṅgehi samannāgato pāpaṇiko bhabbo anadhigataṁ vā bhogaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā bhogaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: A shopkeeper who has these three factors is able to acquire more wealth or to increase the wealth they’ve already acquired.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo anadhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ phātiṁ kātuṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with three qualities is able to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pubbaṇhasamayaṁ sakkaccaṁ samādhinimittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti, majjhanhikasamayaṁ …pe… sāyanhasamayaṁ sakkaccaṁ samādhinimittaṁ adhiṭṭhāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant carefully focuses on a meditation subject as a basis of immersion in the morning, at midday, and in the afternoon.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu bhabbo anadhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ adhigantuṁ, adhigataṁ vā kusalaṁ dhammaṁ phātiṁ kātun”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who possesses these three qualities is able to acquire more skillful qualities or to increase the skillful qualities they’ve already acquired.”
Numbered Discourses 3.20
2. The Chariot-Maker
A Shopkeeper (2nd)

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato pāpaṇiko nacirasseva mahattaṁ vepullattaṁ pāpuṇāti bhogesu.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a shopkeeper who has three factors soon acquires great and abundant wealth.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpaṇiko cakkhumā ca hoti vidhuro ca nissayasampanno ca.
segs.e: It’s when a shopkeeper sees clearly, is indefatigable, and has supporters.
And how does a shopkeeper see clearly?
It’s when a shopkeeper knows of a product:

segs.p: ‘idaṁ paṇiyaṁ evaṁ kītaṁ, evaṁ vikkayamānaṁ, ettakaṁ mūlaṁ bhavissati, ettako udayo’ti.
segs.e: ‘This product is bought at this price and is selling at this price. With this much investment, it’ll bring this much profit.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pāpaṇiko cakkhumā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a shopkeeper sees clearly.
And how is a shopkeeper indefatigable?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpaṇiko kusalo hoti paṇiyaṁ ketuñca vikketuñca.
segs.e: It’s when a shopkeeper is skilled in buying and selling products.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pāpaṇiko vidhuro hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a shopkeeper is indefatigable.
And how does a shopkeeper have supporters?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, pāpaṇikaṁ ye te gahapatī vā gahapatiputtā vā aḍḍhā mahaddhanā mahābhogā te evaṁ jānanti:
segs.e: It’s when rich, affluent, and wealthy householders or householders’ children know of him:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ kho bhavaṁ pāpaṇiko cakkhumā vidhuro ca paṭibalo puttadārañca posetuṁ, amhākañca kālena kālaṁ anuppadātun’ti.
segs.e: ‘This good shopkeeper sees clearly and is indefatigable. They are capable of providing for their wives and children, and paying us back from time to time.’
They deposit money with the shopkeeper, saying:

segs.p: ‘ito, samma pāpaṇika, bhoge karitvā puttadārañca posehi, amhākañca kālena kālaṁ anuppadehī’ti.
segs.e: ‘With this, my good shopkeeper, earn money to provide for your wives and children, and pay us back from time to time.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, pāpaṇiko nissayasampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a shopkeeper has supporters.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi aṅgehi samannāgato pāpaṇiko nacirasseva mahattaṁ vepullattaṁ pāpuṇāti bhogesu.
segs.e: A shopkeeper who has these three factors soon acquires great and abundant wealth.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nacirasseva mahattaṁ vepullattaṁ pāpuṇāti kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with three qualities soon acquires great and abundant skillful qualities.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhumā ca hoti vidhuro ca nissayasampanno ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant sees clearly, is indefatigable, and has supporters.
And how does a mendicant see clearly?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhumā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant sees clearly.
And how is a mendicant indefatigable?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vidhuro hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is indefatigable.
And how does a mendicant have supporters?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā te kālena kālaṁ upasaṅkamitvā paripucchati paripañhati:
segs.e: It’s when from time to time a mendicant goes up to those mendicants who are very learned—inheritors of the heritage, who have memorized the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines—and asks them questions:
‘Why, sir, does it say this? What does that mean?’

segs.p: Tassa te āyasmanto avivaṭañceva vivaranti, anuttānīkatañca uttānīkaronti, anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṁ paṭivinodenti.
segs.e: Those venerables reveal what is hidden, clarify what is unclear, and dispel doubt regarding the many doubtful matters.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu nissayasampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant has supporters.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nacirasseva mahattaṁ vepullattaṁ pāpuṇāti kusalesu dhammesū”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these three qualities soon acquires great and abundant skillful qualities.”
Numbered Discourses 3.21
3. Individuals
With Saviṭṭha
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ca samiddho āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: Then Venerable Saviṭṭha and Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ samiddhaṁ āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side and Venerable Sāriputta said to Venerable Saviṭṭha,

segs.p: “Tayome, āvuso samiddha, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend Saviṭṭha, these three individuals are found in the world.
What three?
The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

segs.p: Ime kho, āvuso, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ, āvuso, tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ katamo te puggalo khamati abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti?
segs.e: Of these three individuals, who do you believe to be the finest?”

segs.p: “Tayome, āvuso sāriputta, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, these three individuals are found in the world.
What three?
The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

segs.p: Ime kho, āvuso, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ, āvuso, tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ yvāyaṁ puggalo saddhāvimutto, ayaṁ me puggalo khamati imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: Of these three individuals, I believe the individual freed by faith to be finest.
Why is that?
Because this individual’s faculty of faith is extraordinary.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ mahākoṭṭhikaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sāriputta said to Mahākoṭṭhita,

segs.p: “tayome, āvuso koṭṭhika, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, these three people are found in the world.
What three?
The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

segs.p: Ime kho, āvuso, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ, āvuso, tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ katamo te puggalo khamati abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti?
segs.e: Of these three individuals, who do you believe to be the finest?”

segs.p: “Tayome, āvuso sāriputta, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, these three individuals are found in the world.
What three?
The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

segs.p: Ime kho, āvuso, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ, āvuso, tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ yvāyaṁ puggalo kāyasakkhī, ayaṁ me puggalo khamati imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: Of these three individuals, I believe the direct witness to be finest.
Why is that?
Because this individual’s faculty of immersion is extraordinary.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahākoṭṭhita said to Sāriputta,

segs.p: “tayome, āvuso sāriputta, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, these three individuals are found in the world.
What three?
The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

segs.p: Ime kho, āvuso, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ, āvuso, tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ katamo te puggalo khamati abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti?
segs.e: Of these three individuals, who do you believe to be the finest?”

segs.p: “Tayome, āvuso koṭṭhika, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend Koṭṭhita, these three people are found in the world.
What three?
The direct witness, the one attained to view, and the one freed by faith.

segs.p: Ime kho, āvuso, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ, āvuso, tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ yvāyaṁ puggalo diṭṭhippatto, ayaṁ me puggalo khamati imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: Of these three individuals, I believe the individual attained to view to be finest.
Why is that?
Because this individual’s faculty of wisdom is extraordinary.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantañca samiddhaṁ āyasmantañca mahākoṭṭhikaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sāriputta said to Saviṭṭha and Mahākoṭṭhita,

segs.p: “byākataṁ kho, āvuso, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakaṁ paṭibhānaṁ.
segs.e: “Each of us has spoken from the heart.

segs.p: Āyāmāvuso, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocessāma.
segs.e: Come, reverends, let’s go to the Buddha, and tell him about this.

segs.p: Yathā no bhagavā byākarissati tathā naṁ dhāressāmā”ti.
segs.e: As he answers, so we’ll remember it.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho āyasmā ca samiddho āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca samiddho āyasmā ca mahākoṭṭhiko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: Then Sāriputta, Saviṭṭha, and Mahākoṭṭhita went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto yāvatako ahosi āyasmatā ca samiddhena āyasmatā ca mahākoṭṭhikena saddhiṁ kathāsallāpo taṁ sabbaṁ bhagavato ārocesi.
segs.e: Then Sāriputta told the Buddha of all they had discussed.
“In this matter, Sāriputta, it’s not easy to categorically declare that

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’ti.
segs.e: one of these three individuals is finest.

segs.p: Ṭhānañhetaṁ, sāriputta, vijjati yvāyaṁ puggalo saddhāvimutto svāssa arahattāya paṭipanno, yvāyaṁ puggalo kāyasakkhī svāssa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā, yo cāyaṁ puggalo diṭṭhippatto sopassa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā.
segs.e: In some cases, an individual freed by faith is practicing for perfection, while the direct witness and the one attained to view are once-returners or non-returners.

segs.p: Na khvettha, sāriputta, sukaraṁ ekaṁsena byākātuṁ:
segs.e: In this matter, it’s not easy to categorically declare that

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’ti.
segs.e: one of these three individuals is finest.

segs.p: Ṭhānañhetaṁ, sāriputta, vijjati yvāyaṁ puggalo kāyasakkhī svāssa arahattāya paṭipanno, yvāyaṁ puggalo saddhāvimutto svāssa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā, yo cāyaṁ puggalo diṭṭhippatto sopassa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā.
segs.e: In some cases, a direct witness is practicing for perfection, while the one freed by faith and the one attained to view are once-returners or non-returners.

segs.p: Na khvettha, sāriputta, sukaraṁ ekaṁsena byākātuṁ:
segs.e: In this matter, it’s not easy to categorically declare that

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’ti.
segs.e: one of these three individuals is finest.

segs.p: Ṭhānañhetaṁ, sāriputta, vijjati yvāyaṁ puggalo diṭṭhippatto svāssa arahattāya paṭipanno, yvāyaṁ puggalo saddhāvimutto svāssa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā, yo cāyaṁ puggalo kāyasakkhī sopassa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā.
segs.e: In some cases, one attained to view is practicing for perfection, while the one freed by faith and the direct witness are once-returners or non-returners.

segs.p: Na khvettha, sāriputta, sukaraṁ ekaṁsena byākātuṁ:
segs.e: In this matter, it’s not easy to categorically declare that

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā’”ti.
segs.e: one of these three individuals is finest.”
Numbered Discourses 3.22
3. Individuals
Patients
“These three patients are found in the world.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco gilāno labhanto vā sappāyāni bhojanāni alabhanto vā sappāyāni bhojanāni, labhanto vā sappāyāni bhesajjāni alabhanto vā sappāyāni bhesajjāni, labhanto vā patirūpaṁ upaṭṭhākaṁ alabhanto vā patirūpaṁ upaṭṭhākaṁ neva vuṭṭhāti tamhā ābādhā.
segs.e: In some cases a patient won’t recover from an illness, regardless of whether or not they get suitable food and medicines, and a capable carer.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco gilāno labhanto vā sappāyāni bhojanāni alabhanto vā sappāyāni bhojanāni, labhanto vā sappāyāni bhesajjāni alabhanto vā sappāyāni bhesajjāni, labhanto vā patirūpaṁ upaṭṭhākaṁ alabhanto vā patirūpaṁ upaṭṭhākaṁ vuṭṭhāti tamhā ābādhā.
segs.e: In some cases a patient will recover from an illness, regardless of whether or not they get suitable food and medicines, and a capable carer.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco gilāno labhantova sappāyāni bhojanāni no alabhanto, labhantova sappāyāni bhesajjāni no alabhanto, labhantova patirūpaṁ upaṭṭhākaṁ no alabhanto vuṭṭhāti tamhā ābādhā.
segs.e: In some cases a patient can recover from an illness, but only if they get suitable food and medicines, and a capable carer, and not if they don’t get these things.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ gilāno labhantova sappāyāni bhojanāni no alabhanto, labhantova sappāyāni bhesajjāni no alabhanto, labhantova patirūpaṁ upaṭṭhākaṁ no alabhanto vuṭṭhāti tamhā ābādhā, imaṁ kho, bhikkhave, gilānaṁ paṭicca gilānabhattaṁ anuññātaṁ gilānabhesajjaṁ anuññātaṁ gilānupaṭṭhāko anuññāto.
segs.e: Now, it’s for the sake of the last patient—who will recover only if they get suitable food and medicines, and a capable carer—that food, medicines, and a carer are prescribed.

segs.p: Imañca pana, bhikkhave, gilānaṁ paṭicca aññepi gilānā upaṭṭhātabbā.
segs.e: But also, for the sake of this patient, the other patients should be looked after.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo gilānā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the three kinds of patients found in the world.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tayome gilānūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, these three individuals similar to patients are found in the world.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo labhanto vā tathāgataṁ dassanāya alabhanto vā tathāgataṁ dassanāya, labhanto vā tathāgatappaveditaṁ dhammavinayaṁ savanāya alabhanto vā tathāgatappaveditaṁ dhammavinayaṁ savanāya neva okkamati niyāmaṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Some people don’t step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, regardless of whether or not they get to see a Realized One, and to hear the teaching and training that he proclaims.

segs.p: Idha, pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo labhanto vā tathāgataṁ dassanāya alabhanto vā tathāgataṁ dassanāya, labhanto vā tathāgatappaveditaṁ dhammavinayaṁ savanāya alabhanto vā tathāgatappaveditaṁ dhammavinayaṁ savanāya okkamati niyāmaṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Some people do step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, regardless of whether or not they get to see a Realized One, and to hear the teaching and training that he proclaims.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo labhantova tathāgataṁ dassanāya no alabhanto, labhantova tathāgatappaveditaṁ dhammavinayaṁ savanāya no alabhanto okkamati niyāmaṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ.
segs.e: Some people can step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, but only if they get to see a Realized One, and to hear the teaching and training that he proclaims, and not when they don’t get those things.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo labhantova tathāgataṁ dassanāya no alabhanto, labhantova tathāgatappaveditaṁ dhammavinayaṁ savanāya no alabhanto okkamati niyāmaṁ kusalesu dhammesu sammattaṁ, imaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalaṁ paṭicca dhammadesanā anuññātā.
segs.e: Now, it’s for the sake of this last individual that teaching the Dhamma is prescribed, that is, the one who can step into the sure path with regard to skillful qualities, but only if they get to see a Realized One, and to hear the teaching and training that he proclaims.

segs.p: Imañca pana, bhikkhave, puggalaṁ paṭicca aññesampi dhammo desetabbo.
segs.e: But also, for the sake of this individual, the other people should be taught Dhamma.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo gilānūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the three individuals similar to patients found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 3.23
3. Individuals
Choices
“These three individuals are found in the world.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sabyābajjhaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhaṁ vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhaṁ manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti.
segs.e: Firstly, a certain individual makes hurtful choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So sabyābajjhaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhaṁ vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhaṁ manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharitvā sabyābajjhaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Having made these choices, they’re reborn in a hurtful world,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ sabyābajjhaṁ lokaṁ upapannaṁ samānaṁ sabyābajjhā phassā phusanti.
segs.e: where hurtful contacts strike them.

segs.p: So sabyābajjhehi phassehi phuṭṭho samāno sabyābajjhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayati ekantadukkhaṁ, seyyathāpi sattā nerayikā.
segs.e: Touched by hurtful contacts, they experience hurtful feelings that are absolutely painful—like the beings in hell.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo abyābajjhaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, abyābajjhaṁ vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, abyābajjhaṁ manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, another individual makes pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So abyābajjhaṁ kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharitvā, abyābajjhaṁ vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharitvā, abyābajjhaṁ manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharitvā abyābajjhaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Having made these choices, they are reborn in a pleasing world,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ abyābajjhaṁ lokaṁ upapannaṁ samānaṁ abyābajjhā phassā phusanti.
segs.e: where pleasing contacts strike them.

segs.p: So abyābajjhehi phassehi phuṭṭho samāno abyābajjhaṁ vedanaṁ vedayati ekantasukhaṁ, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā.
segs.e: Touched by pleasing contacts, they experience pleasing feelings of absolute happiness—like the gods of universal beauty.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, another individual makes both hurtful and pleasing choices by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharitvā, sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharitvā sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: Having made these choices, they are reborn in a world that is both hurtful and pleasing,

segs.p: Tamenaṁ sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi lokaṁ upapannaṁ samānaṁ sabyābajjhāpi abyābajjhāpi phassā phusanti.
segs.e: where hurtful and pleasing contacts strike them.

segs.p: So sabyābajjhehipi abyābajjhehipi phassehi phuṭṭho samāno sabyābajjhampi abyābajjhampi vedanaṁ vedayati vokiṇṇasukhadukkhaṁ, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā.
segs.e: Touched by both hurtful and pleasing contacts, they experience both hurtful and pleasing feelings that are a mixture of pleasure and pain—like humans, some gods, and some beings in the underworld.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 3.24
3. Individuals
Very Helpful
“Mendicants, these three individuals are very helpful to another.
What three?

segs.p: Yaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalaṁ āgamma puggalo buddhaṁ saraṇaṁ gato hoti, dhammaṁ saraṇaṁ gato hoti, saṅghaṁ saraṇaṁ gato hoti;
segs.e: The individual who has enabled you to go for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.

segs.p: ayaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalo imassa puggalassa bahukāro.
segs.e: This individual is very helpful to another.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yaṁ puggalaṁ āgamma puggalo ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti;
segs.e: Furthermore, the individual who has enabled you to truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: ayaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalo imassa puggalassa bahukāro.
segs.e: This individual is very helpful to another.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yaṁ puggalaṁ āgamma puggalo āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: Furthermore, the individual who has enabled you to realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with your own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: ayaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalo imassa puggalassa bahukāro.
segs.e: This individual is very helpful to another.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā puggalassa bahukārā.
segs.e: These are the three individuals who are very helpful to another individual.

segs.p: Imehi ca pana, bhikkhave, tīhi puggalehi imassa puggalassa natthañño puggalo bahukāroti vadāmi.
segs.e: And I say that there is no one more helpful to another than these three individuals.

segs.p: Imesaṁ pana, bhikkhave, tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ iminā puggalena na suppatikāraṁ vadāmi, yadidaṁ abhivādanapaccuṭṭhānaañjalikammasāmīcikammacīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānuppadānenā”ti.
segs.e: And I also say that it’s not easy to repay these three individuals by bowing down to them, rising up for them, greeting them with cupped palms, and observing proper etiquette for them; or by providing them with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.”
Numbered Discourses 3.25
3. Individuals
Like Diamond
“These three individuals are found in the world.
What three?

segs.p: Arukūpamacitto puggalo, vijjūpamacitto puggalo, vajirūpamacitto puggalo.
segs.e: An individual with a mind like an open sore, an individual with a mind like lightning, and an individual with a mind like diamond.
And who has a mind like an open sore?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo kodhano hoti upāyāsabahulo
segs.e: It’s an individual who is irritable and bad-tempered.

segs.p: appampi vutto samāno abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patitthīyati kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: Even when lightly criticized they lose their temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and they display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, duṭṭhāruko kaṭṭhena vā kaṭhalāya vā ghaṭṭito bhiyyoso mattāya āsavaṁ deti;
segs.e: They’re like a festering sore, which, when you hit it with a stick or a stone, discharges even more.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo kodhano hoti upāyāsabahulo
segs.e: In the same way, an individual is irritable and bad-tempered.

segs.p: appampi vutto samāno abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patitthīyati kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: Even when lightly criticized they lose their temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and they display annoyance, hate, and bitterness.
This is called an individual with a mind like an open sore.
And who has a mind like lightning?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s an individual who truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, cakkhumā puriso rattandhakāratimisāyaṁ vijjantarikāya rūpāni passeyya;
segs.e: They’re like a person with keen eyes in the dark of the night, who sees by a flash of lightning.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: In the same way, an individual truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.
This is called an individual with a mind like lightning.
And who has a mind like diamond?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s an individual who realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vajirassa natthi kiñci abhejjaṁ maṇi vā pāsāṇo vā;
segs.e: It’s like a diamond, which can’t be cut by anything at all, not even a gem or a stone.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: In the same way, an individual realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …
This is called an individual with a mind like diamond.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 3.26
3. Individuals
Associates
“These three individuals are found in the world.
What three?

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, puggalo na sevitabbo na bhajitabbo na payirupāsitabbo.
segs.e: There is an individual you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend.

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, puggalo sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo.
segs.e: There is an individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend.

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, puggalo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo.
segs.e: There is an individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend with honor and respect.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo na sevitabbo na bhajitabbo na payirupāsitabbo?
segs.e: Who is the individual you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo hīno hoti sīlena samādhinā paññāya.
segs.e: It’s an individual who is inferior in terms of ethics, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: Evarūpo, bhikkhave, puggalo na sevitabbo na bhajitabbo na payirupāsitabbo aññatra anuddayā aññatra anukampā.
segs.e: You shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend such an individual, except out of kindness and sympathy.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo?
segs.e: Who is the individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sadiso hoti sīlena samādhinā paññāya.
segs.e: It’s an individual who is similar in terms of ethics, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: Evarūpo, bhikkhave, puggalo sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo.
segs.e: You should associate with, accompany, and attend such an individual.
Why is that?

segs.p: Sīlasāmaññagatānaṁ sataṁ sīlakathā ca no bhavissati, sā ca no pavattinī bhavissati, sā ca no phāsu bhavissati.
segs.e: Thinking, ‘Since our ethical conduct is similar, we can discuss ethics, the conversation will flow, and we’ll both be at ease.

segs.p: Samādhisāmaññagatānaṁ sataṁ samādhikathā ca no bhavissati, sā ca no pavattinī bhavissati, sā ca no phāsu bhavissati.
segs.e: Since our immersion is similar, we can discuss immersion, the conversation will flow, and we’ll both be at ease.

segs.p: Paññāsāmaññagatānaṁ sataṁ paññākathā ca no bhavissati, sā ca no pavattinī bhavissati, sā ca no phāsu bhavissatīti.
segs.e: Since our wisdom is similar, we can discuss wisdom, the conversation will flow, and we’ll both be at ease.’

segs.p: Tasmā evarūpo puggalo sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo.
segs.e: That’s why you should associate with, accompany, and attend such an individual.

segs.p: Katamo ca, bhikkhave, puggalo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo?
segs.e: Who is the individual you should associate with, accompany, and attend with honor and respect?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo adhiko hoti sīlena samādhinā paññāya.
segs.e: It’s an individual who is superior in terms of ethics, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: Evarūpo, bhikkhave, puggalo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo.
segs.e: You should associate with, accompany, and attend such an individual with honor and respect.
Why is that?

segs.p: Iti aparipūraṁ vā sīlakkhandhaṁ paripūressāmi, paripūraṁ vā sīlakkhandhaṁ tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmi;
segs.e: Thinking, ‘I’ll fulfill the entire spectrum of ethical conduct I haven’t yet fulfilled, or support with wisdom in every situation the ethical conduct I’ve already fulfilled.

segs.p: aparipūraṁ vā samādhikkhandhaṁ paripūressāmi, paripūraṁ vā samādhikkhandhaṁ tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmi;
segs.e: I’ll fulfill the entire spectrum of immersion I haven’t yet fulfilled, or support with wisdom in every situation the immersion I’ve already fulfilled.

segs.p: aparipūraṁ vā paññākkhandhaṁ paripūressāmi, paripūraṁ vā paññākkhandhaṁ tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmīti.
segs.e: I’ll fulfill the entire spectrum of wisdom I haven’t yet fulfilled, or support with wisdom in every situation the wisdom I’ve already fulfilled.’

segs.p: Tasmā evarūpo puggalo sakkatvā garuṁ katvā sevitabbo bhajitabbo payirupāsitabbo.
segs.e: That’s why you should associate with, accompany, and attend this individual with honor and respect.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasminti.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.
A man who associates with an inferior goes downhill,
but associating with an equal, you’ll never decline;
following the best, you’ll quickly rise up,
so you should keep company <j>with people better than you.”
Numbered Discourses 3.27
3. Individuals
You Should be Disgusted
“These three individuals are found in the world.
What three?

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, puggalo jigucchitabbo na sevitabbo na bhajitabbo na payirupāsitabbo.
segs.e: There is an individual you should be disgusted by, and you shouldn’t associate with, accompany, or attend them.
