segs.e: When you apply the mind irrationally to the feature of aversion, hate arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena anuppanno vā doso uppajjati uppanno vā doso bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī’ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why hate arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.’

segs.p: ‘Ko panāvuso, hetu ko paccayo yena anuppanno vā moho uppajjati uppanno vā moho bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī’ti?
segs.e: And if they ask: ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why delusion arises, and once arisen it increases and grows?’
You should say: ‘Irrational application of mind.

segs.p: Tassa ayoniso manasi karoto anuppanno vā moho uppajjati uppanno vā moho bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: When you apply the mind irrationally, delusion arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena anuppanno vā moho uppajjati uppanno vā moho bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṁvattatī’ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why delusion arises, and once arisen it increases and grows.’

segs.p: ‘Ko panāvuso, hetu ko paccayo yena anuppanno ceva rāgo nuppajjati uppanno ca rāgo pahīyatī’ti?
segs.e: And if they ask, ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why greed doesn’t arise, or if it’s already arisen it’s given up?’
You should say: ‘The feature of ugliness.

segs.p: Tassa asubhanimittaṁ yoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva rāgo nuppajjati uppanno ca rāgo pahīyati.
segs.e: When you apply the mind rationally on the ugly feature of things, greed doesn’t arise, or if it’s already arisen it’s given up.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena anuppanno ceva rāgo nuppajjati uppanno ca rāgo pahīyatī’ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why greed doesn’t arise, or if it’s already arisen it’s given up.’

segs.p: ‘Ko panāvuso, hetu ko paccayo yena anuppanno ceva doso nuppajjati uppanno ca doso pahīyatī’ti?
segs.e: And if they ask, ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why hate doesn’t arise, or if it’s already arisen it’s given up?’
You should say: ‘The heart’s release by love.

segs.p: Tassa mettaṁ cetovimuttiṁ yoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva doso nuppajjati uppanno ca doso pahīyati.
segs.e: When you apply the mind rationally on the heart’s release by love, hate doesn’t arise, or if it’s already arisen it’s given up.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena anuppanno ceva doso nuppajjati uppanno ca doso pahīyatī’ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why hate doesn’t arise, or if it’s already arisen it’s given up.’

segs.p: ‘Ko panāvuso, hetu ko paccayo yena anuppanno ceva moho nuppajjati uppanno ca moho pahīyatī’ti?
segs.e: And if they ask, ‘What is the cause, what is the reason why delusion doesn’t arise, or if it’s already arisen it’s given up?’
You should say: ‘Rational application of mind.

segs.p: Tassa yoniso manasi karoto anuppanno ceva moho nuppajjati uppanno ca moho pahīyati.
segs.e: When you apply the mind rationally, delusion doesn’t arise, or if it’s already arisen it’s given up.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, hetu ayaṁ paccayo yena anuppanno vā moho nuppajjati uppanno ca moho pahīyatī’”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why delusion doesn’t arise, or if it’s already arisen it’s given up.’”
Numbered Discourses 3.69
7. The Great Chapter
Unskillful Roots
“Mendicants, there are these three unskillful roots.
What three?

segs.p: Lobho akusalamūlaṁ, doso akusalamūlaṁ, moho akusalamūlaṁ.
segs.e: Greed, hate, and delusion.
Greed is a root of the unskillful.

segs.p: yadapi luddho abhisaṅkharoti kāyena vācāya manasā tadapi akusalaṁ;
segs.e: When a greedy person chooses to act by way of body, speech, or mind, that too is unskillful.

segs.p: yadapi luddho lobhena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto parassa asatā dukkhaṁ uppādayati vadhena vā bandhanena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā pabbājanāya vā balavamhi balattho itipi tadapi akusalaṁ.
segs.e: When a greedy person, overcome by greed, causes another to suffer under a false pretext—by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment—thinking ‘I’m powerful, I want power’, that too is unskillful.

segs.p: Itissame lobhajā lobhanidānā lobhasamudayā lobhapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti.
segs.e: And so these many bad, unskillful things are produced in them, born, sourced, originated, and conditioned by greed.
Hate is a root of the unskillful.

segs.p: yadapi duṭṭho abhisaṅkharoti kāyena vācāya manasā tadapi akusalaṁ;
segs.e: When a hateful person chooses to act by way of body, speech, or mind, that too is unskillful.

segs.p: yadapi duṭṭho dosena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto parassa asatā dukkhaṁ uppādayati vadhena vā bandhanena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā pabbājanāya vā balavamhi balattho itipi tadapi akusalaṁ.
segs.e: When a hateful person, overcome by hate, causes another to suffer under a false pretext—by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment—thinking ‘I’m powerful, I want power’, that too is unskillful.

segs.p: Itissame dosajā dosanidānā dosasamudayā dosapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti.
segs.e: And so these many bad, unskillful things are produced in them, born, sourced, originated, and conditioned by hate.
Delusion is a root of the unskillful.

segs.p: yadapi mūḷho abhisaṅkharoti kāyena vācāya manasā tadapi akusalaṁ;
segs.e: When a deluded person chooses to act by way of body, speech, or mind, that too is unskillful.

segs.p: yadapi mūḷho mohena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto parassa asatā dukkhaṁ uppādayati vadhena vā bandhanena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā pabbājanāya vā balavamhi balattho itipi tadapi akusalaṁ.
segs.e: When a deluded person, overcome by delusion, causes another to suffer under a false pretext—by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment—thinking ‘I’m powerful, I want power’, that too is unskillful.

segs.p: Itissame mohajā mohanidānā mohasamudayā mohapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti.
segs.e: And so these many bad, unskillful things are produced in them, born, sourced, originated, and conditioned by delusion.

segs.p: Evarūpo cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalo vuccati akālavādītipi, abhūtavādītipi, anatthavādītipi, adhammavādītipi, avinayavādītipi.
segs.e: Such an individual is said to have speech that’s ill-timed, false, meaningless, not in line with the teaching and training.

segs.p: Kasmā cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, evarūpo puggalo vuccati akālavādītipi, abhūtavādītipi, anatthavādītipi, adhammavādītipi, avinayavādītipi?
segs.e: Why is this?

segs.p: Tathāhāyaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalo parassa asatā dukkhaṁ uppādayati vadhena vā bandhanena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā pabbājanāya vā balavamhi balattho itipi.
segs.e: This individual causes another to suffer under a false pretext—by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment—thinking ‘I’m powerful, I want power’.

segs.p: Bhūtena kho pana vuccamāno avajānāti, no paṭijānāti;
segs.e: So when someone makes a valid criticism, they’re scornful and admit nothing.

segs.p: abhūtena vuccamāno na ātappaṁ karoti, tassa nibbeṭhanāya itipetaṁ atacchaṁ itipetaṁ abhūtanti.
segs.e: When someone makes a baseless criticism, they make no effort to explain, ‘This is why that’s untrue, this is why that’s false.’

segs.p: Tasmā evarūpo puggalo vuccati akālavādītipi, abhūtavādītipi, anatthavādītipi, adhammavādītipi, avinayavādītipi.
segs.e: That’s why such an individual is said to have speech that’s ill-timed, false, meaningless, not in line with the teaching and training.

segs.p: Evarūpo, bhikkhave, puggalo lobhajehi pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto diṭṭhe ceva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharati, savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ.
segs.e: Such an individual—overcome with bad, unskillful qualities born of greed, hate, and delusion—suffers in this very life, with distress, anguish, and fever.

segs.p: Kāyassa ca bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: And when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect to be reborn in a bad place.

segs.p: mohajehi pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto diṭṭhe ceva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharati, savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ.
Kāyassa ca bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.
Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sālo vā dhavo vā phandano vā tīhi māluvālatāhi uddhasto pariyonaddho anayaṁ āpajjati, byasanaṁ āpajjati, anayabyasanaṁ āpajjati;
segs.e: Suppose a sal, axlewood, or sandan tree was choked and enveloped by three camel’s foot creepers. It would fall to ruin and disaster.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, evarūpo puggalo lobhajehi pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto diṭṭhe ceva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharati, savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, such an individual—overcome with bad, unskillful qualities born of greed, hate, and delusion—suffers in this very life, with distress, anguish, and fever.

segs.p: Kāyassa ca bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: And when the body breaks up, after death, they can expect to be reborn in a bad place.

segs.p: mohajehi pāpakehi akusalehi dhammehi abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto diṭṭhe ceva dhamme dukkhaṁ viharati savighātaṁ saupāyāsaṁ sapariḷāhaṁ.
Kāyassa ca bhedā paraṁ maraṇā duggati pāṭikaṅkhā.

segs.e: These are the three unskillful roots.
There are these three skillful roots.
What three?

segs.p: Alobho kusalamūlaṁ, adoso kusalamūlaṁ, amoho kusalamūlaṁ.
segs.e: Contentment, love, and understanding.
Contentment is a root of the skillful.

segs.p: yadapi aluddho abhisaṅkharoti kāyena vācāya manasā tadapi kusalaṁ;
segs.e: When a contented person chooses to act by way of body, speech, or mind, that too is skillful.

segs.p: yadapi aluddho lobhena anabhibhūto apariyādinnacitto na parassa asatā dukkhaṁ uppādayati vadhena vā bandhanena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā pabbājanāya vā balavamhi balattho itipi tadapi kusalaṁ.
segs.e: When a contented person, not overcome by greed, doesn’t cause another to suffer under a false pretext—by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment—thinking ‘I’m powerful, I want power’, that too is skillful.

segs.p: Itissame alobhajā alobhanidānā alobhasamudayā alobhapaccayā aneke kusalā dhammā sambhavanti.
segs.e: And so these many skillful things are produced in them, born, sourced, originated, and conditioned by contentment.
Love is a root of the skillful.

segs.p: yadapi aduṭṭho abhisaṅkharoti kāyena vācāya manasā tadapi kusalaṁ;
segs.e: When a loving person chooses to act by way of body, speech, or mind, that too is skillful.

segs.p: yadapi aduṭṭho dosena anabhibhūto apariyādinnacitto na parassa asatā dukkhaṁ uppādayati vadhena vā bandhanena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā pabbājanāya vā balavamhi balattho itipi tadapi kusalaṁ.
segs.e: When a loving person, not overcome by hate, doesn’t cause another to suffer under a false pretext—by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment—thinking ‘I’m powerful, I want power’, that too is skillful.

segs.p: Itissame adosajā adosanidānā adosasamudayā adosapaccayā aneke kusalā dhammā sambhavanti.
segs.e: And so these many skillful things are produced in them, born, sourced, originated, and conditioned by love.
Understanding is a root of the skillful.

segs.p: yadapi amūḷho abhisaṅkharoti kāyena vācāya manasā tadapi kusalaṁ;
segs.e: When an understanding person chooses to act by way of body, speech, or mind, that too is skillful.

segs.p: yadapi amūḷho mohena anabhibhūto apariyādinnacitto na parassa asatā dukkhaṁ uppādayati vadhena vā bandhanena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā pabbājanāya vā balavamhi balattho itipi tadapi kusalaṁ.
segs.e: When an understanding person, not overcome by delusion, doesn’t cause another to suffer under a false pretext—by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment—thinking ‘I’m powerful, I want power’, that too is skillful.

segs.p: Itissame amohajā amohanidānā amohasamudayā amohapaccayā aneke kusalā dhammā sambhavanti.
segs.e: And so these many skillful things are produced in them, born, sourced, originated, and conditioned by understanding.

segs.p: Evarūpo cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalo vuccati kālavādītipi, bhūtavādītipi, atthavādītipi, dhammavādītipi, vinayavādītipi.
segs.e: Such an individual is said to have speech that’s well-timed, true, meaningful, in line with the teaching and training.

segs.p: Kasmā cāyaṁ, bhikkhave, evarūpo puggalo vuccati kālavādītipi, bhūtavādītipi, atthavādītipi, dhammavādītipi, vinayavādītipi?
segs.e: Why is this?

segs.p: Tathāhāyaṁ, bhikkhave, puggalo na parassa asatā dukkhaṁ uppādayati vadhena vā bandhanena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā pabbājanāya vā balavamhi balattho itipi.
segs.e: This individual doesn’t cause another to suffer under a false pretext—by execution or imprisonment or confiscation or condemnation or banishment—thinking ‘I’m powerful, I want power’.

segs.p: Bhūtena kho pana vuccamāno paṭijānāti no avajānāti;
segs.e: So when someone makes a valid criticism, they admit it and aren’t scornful.

segs.p: abhūtena vuccamāno ātappaṁ karoti tassa nibbeṭhanāya:
segs.e: When someone makes a baseless criticism, they make an effort to explain,
‘This is why that’s untrue, this is why that’s false.’

segs.p: Tasmā evarūpo puggalo vuccati kālavādītipi, atthavādītipi, dhammavādītipi, vinayavādītipi.
segs.e: That’s why such an individual is said to have speech that’s well-timed, true, meaningful, in line with the teaching and training.

segs.p: Evarūpassa, bhikkhave, puggalassa lobhajā pāpakā akusalā dhammā pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: For such an individual, bad unskillful qualities born of greed, hate, and delusion are cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṁ viharati avighātaṁ anupāyāsaṁ apariḷāhaṁ.
segs.e: In this very life they’re happy, free of distress, anguish, and fever,
and they’re also extinguished in this very life.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi bhikkhave, sālo vā dhavo vā phandano vā tīhi māluvālatāhi uddhasto pariyonaddho.
segs.e: Suppose a sal, axlewood, or sandan tree was choked and enveloped by three camel’s foot creepers.
Then along comes a person with a spade and basket.

segs.p: So taṁ māluvālataṁ mūle chindeyya, mūle chetvā palikhaṇeyya, palikhaṇitvā mūlāni uddhareyya, antamaso usīranāḷimattānipi.
segs.e: They’d cut the creeper out by the roots, dig them up, and pull them out, down to the fibers and stems.

segs.p: So taṁ māluvālataṁ khaṇḍākhaṇḍikaṁ chindeyya, khaṇḍākhaṇḍikaṁ chetvā phāleyya, phāletvā sakalikaṁ sakalikaṁ kareyya, sakalikaṁ sakalikaṁ karitvā vātātape visoseyya, vātātape visosetvā agginā ḍaheyya, agginā ḍahitvā masiṁ kareyya, masiṁ karitvā mahāvāte vā ophuṇeyya nadiyā vā sīghasotāya pavāheyya.
segs.e: Then they’d split the creeper apart, cut up the parts, and chop it into splinters. They’d dry the splinters in the wind and sun, burn them with fire, and reduce them to ashes. Then they’d whisk away the ashes in a strong wind, or glide them down a swift stream.

segs.p: Evamassa tā, bhikkhave, māluvālatā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: So those camel’s foot creepers would be cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, and obliterated, unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, evarūpassa puggalassa lobhajā pāpakā akusalā dhammā pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: In the same way, for such an individual, bad unskillful qualities born of greed, hate, and delusion are cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṁ viharati avighātaṁ anupāyāsaṁ apariḷāhaṁ.
segs.e: In this very life they’re happy, free of  distress, anguish, and fever,
and they’re also extinguished in this very life.

segs.p: mohajā pāpakā akusalā dhammā pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
Diṭṭheva dhamme sukhaṁ viharati avighātaṁ anupāyāsaṁ apariḷāhaṁ.

segs.e: These are the three skillful roots.”
Numbered Discourses 3.70
7. The Great Chapter
Sabbath
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho visākhā migāramātā tadahuposathe yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho visākhaṁ migāramātaraṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Visākhā, Migāra’s mother, went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to her,

segs.p: “handa kuto nu tvaṁ, visākhe, āgacchasi divā divassā”ti?
segs.e: “So, Visākhā, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”
“Today, sir, I’m observing the sabbath.”
“There are, Visākhā, these three sabbaths.
What three?
The sabbath of the cowherds, the sabbath of the Jains, and the sabbath of the noble ones.
And what is the sabbath of the cowherds?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, visākhe, gopālako sāyanhasamaye sāmikānaṁ gāvo niyyātetvā iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: It’s just like a cowherd who, in the late afternoon, takes the cows back to their owners. They reflect:

segs.p: ‘ajja kho gāvo amukasmiñca amukasmiñca padese cariṁsu, amukasmiñca amukasmiñca padese pānīyāni piviṁsu;
segs.e: ‘Today the cows grazed in this spot and that, and they drank in this spot and that.

segs.p: sve dāni gāvo amukasmiñca amukasmiñca padese carissanti, amukasmiñca amukasmiñca padese pānīyāni pivissantī’ti;
segs.e: Tomorrow the cows will graze in this spot and that, and drink in this spot and that.’

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, visākhe, idhekacco uposathiko iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: In the same way, someone keeping the sabbath reflects:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ khvajja idañcidañca khādanīyaṁ khādiṁ, idañcidañca bhojanīyaṁ bhuñjiṁ;
segs.e: ‘Today I ate this and that, and had a meal of this and that.

segs.p: sve dānāhaṁ idañcidañca khādanīyaṁ khādissāmi, idañcidañca bhojanīyaṁ bhuñjissāmī’ti.
segs.e: Tomorrow I’ll eat this and that, and have a meal of this and that.’

segs.p: So tena abhijjhāsahagatena cetasā divasaṁ atināmeti.
segs.e: And so they spend their day with a mind full of covetousness.
That’s the sabbath of the cowherds.

segs.p: Evaṁ upavuttho kho, visākhe, gopālakuposatho na mahapphalo hoti na mahānisaṁso na mahājutiko na mahāvipphāro.
segs.e: When the cowherd’s sabbath is observed like this it’s not very fruitful or beneficial or brilliant or bountiful.
And what is the sabbath of the Jains?
There’s a kind of ascetic belonging to a group called the Jains.
They encourage their disciple:

segs.p: ‘ehi tvaṁ, ambho purisa, ye puratthimāya disāya pāṇā paraṁ yojanasataṁ tesu daṇḍaṁ nikkhipāhi;
segs.e: ‘Please, my man, don’t hurt any living creatures more than a hundred leagues away to the east.

segs.p: ye pacchimāya disāya pāṇā paraṁ yojanasataṁ tesu daṇḍaṁ nikkhipāhi;
segs.e: Don’t hurt any living creatures more than a hundred leagues away to the west.

segs.p: ye uttarāya disāya pāṇā paraṁ yojanasataṁ tesu daṇḍaṁ nikkhipāhi;
segs.e: Don’t hurt any living creatures more than a hundred leagues away to the north.

segs.p: ye dakkhiṇāya disāya pāṇā paraṁ yojanasataṁ tesu daṇḍaṁ nikkhipāhī’ti.
segs.e: Don’t hurt any living creatures more than a hundred leagues away to the south.’

segs.p: Iti ekaccānaṁ pāṇānaṁ anuddayāya anukampāya samādapenti, ekaccānaṁ pāṇānaṁ nānuddayāya nānukampāya samādapenti.
segs.e: So they encourage kindness and sympathy for some creatures and not others.
On the sabbath, they encourage their disciple:

segs.p: ‘ehi tvaṁ, ambho purisa, sabbacelāni nikkhipitvā evaṁ vadehi—
segs.e: ‘Please, my man, take off all your clothes and say:

segs.p: nāhaṁ kvacani kassaci kiñcanatasmiṁ, na ca mama kvacani katthaci kiñcanatatthī’ti.
segs.e: “I don’t belong to anyone anywhere! And nothing belongs to me anywhere!”’
But their mother and father still know,
‘This is our child.’
And they know,
‘This is my mother and father.’
Partner and child still know,
‘This is our supporter.’
And they know,
‘This is my partner and child.’
Bondservants, workers, and staff still know:
‘This is our master.’
And they know,
‘These are my bondservants, workers, and staff.’

segs.p: Iti yasmiṁ samaye sacce samādapetabbā musāvāde tasmiṁ samaye samādapenti.
segs.e: So, at a time when they should be encouraged to speak the truth, the Jains encourage them to lie.
This, I say, is lying.

segs.p: So tassā rattiyā accayena bhoge adinnaṁyeva paribhuñjati.
segs.e: When the night has passed they use their possessions once more, though they’ve not been given back to them.
This, I say, is stealing.
That’s the sabbath of the Jains.

segs.p: Evaṁ upavuttho kho, visākhe, nigaṇṭhuposatho na mahapphalo hoti na mahānisaṁso na mahājutiko na mahāvipphāro.
segs.e: When the Jain’s sabbath is observed like this it’s not very fruitful or beneficial or brilliant or bountiful.
And what is the sabbath of the noble ones?

segs.p: Upakkiliṭṭhassa, visākhe, cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: A corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?
It’s when a noble disciple recollects the Realized One:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Tassa tathāgataṁ anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti, seyyathāpi, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa sīsassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: As they recollect the Realized One, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up. It’s just like cleaning a dirty head by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa sīsassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a dirty head cleaned by exertion?

segs.p: Kakkañca paṭicca mattikañca paṭicca udakañca paṭicca purisassa ca tajjaṁ vāyāmaṁ paṭicca, evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa sīsassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: With cleansing paste, clay, and water, and by applying the appropriate effort.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: In the same way, a corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?
It’s when a noble disciple recollects the Realized One:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Tassa tathāgataṁ anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti.
segs.e: As they recollect the Realized One, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.
This is called:

segs.p: ‘ariyasāvako brahmuposathaṁ upavasati, brahmunā saddhiṁ saṁvasati, brahmañcassa ārabbha cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti’.
segs.e: ‘A noble disciple who observes the sabbath of the divinity, living together with the divinity. And because they think of the divinity their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Upakkiliṭṭhassa, visākhe, cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: A corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?
It’s when a noble disciple recollects the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Tassa dhammaṁ anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti, seyyathāpi, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa kāyassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: As they recollect the teaching, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up. It’s just like cleaning a dirty body by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa kāyassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a dirty body cleaned by exertion?

segs.p: Sottiñca paṭicca, cuṇṇañca paṭicca, udakañca paṭicca, purisassa ca tajjaṁ vāyāmaṁ paṭicca.
segs.e: With cleanser and powder, water, and by applying the appropriate effort.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa kāyassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a dirty body is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: In the same way, a corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?
It’s when a noble disciple recollects the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Tassa dhammaṁ anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti.
segs.e: As they recollect the teaching, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, visākhe, ‘ariyasāvako dhammuposathaṁ upavasati, dhammena saddhiṁ saṁvasati, dhammañcassa ārabbha cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti’.
segs.e: This is called: ‘A noble disciple who observes the sabbath of Dhamma, living together with Dhamma. And because they think of the Dhamma their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Upakkiliṭṭhassa, visākhe, cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: A corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?
It’s when a noble disciple recollects the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Tassa saṅghaṁ anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti, seyyathāpi, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa vatthassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: As they recollect the Saṅgha, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up. It’s just like cleaning a dirty cloth by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa vatthassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a dirty cloth cleaned by applying effort?

segs.p: Usmañca paṭicca, khārañca paṭicca, gomayañca paṭicca, udakañca paṭicca, purisassa ca tajjaṁ vāyāmaṁ paṭicca.
segs.e: With salt, lye, cow dung, and water, and by applying the appropriate effort.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa vatthassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a dirty cloth is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: In the same way, a corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?
It’s when a noble disciple recollects the Saṅgha:

‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, and worthy of veneration with cupped palms. It is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Tassa saṅghaṁ anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti.
segs.e: As they recollect the Saṅgha, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, visākhe, ‘ariyasāvako saṅghuposathaṁ upavasati, saṅghena saddhiṁ saṁvasati, saṅghañcassa ārabbha cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti’.
segs.e: This is called: ‘A noble disciple who observes the sabbath of the Saṅgha, living together with the Saṅgha. And because they think of the Saṅgha their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Upakkiliṭṭhassa, visākhe, cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: A corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, ariyasāvako attano sīlāni anussarati akhaṇḍāni acchiddāni asabalāni akammāsāni bhujissāni viññuppasatthāni aparāmaṭṭhāni samādhisaṁvattanikāni.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple recollects their own ethical precepts, which are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Tassa sīlaṁ anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti, seyyathāpi, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa ādāsassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: As they recollect their ethical conduct, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up. It’s just like cleaning a dirty mirror by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa ādāsassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a dirty mirror cleaned by exertion?

segs.p: Telañca paṭicca, chārikañca paṭicca, vālaṇḍupakañca paṭicca, purisassa ca tajjaṁ vāyāmaṁ paṭicca.
segs.e: With oil, ash, a rolled-up cloth, and by applying the appropriate effort.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa ādāsassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a dirty mirror is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: In the same way, a corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?

segs.p: Idha, visākhe, ariyasāvako attano sīlāni anussarati akhaṇḍāni …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikāni.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple recollects their own ethical precepts, which are intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Tassa sīlaṁ anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti.
segs.e: As they recollect their ethical conduct, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, visākhe, ‘ariyasāvako sīluposathaṁ upavasati, sīlena saddhiṁ saṁvasati, sīlañcassa ārabbha cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti’.
segs.e: This is called: ‘A noble disciple who observes the sabbath of ethical conduct, living together with ethics. And because they think of their ethical conduct their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Upakkiliṭṭhassa, visākhe, cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: A corrupt mind is cleaned by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?
It’s when a noble disciple recollects the deities:

segs.p: ‘santi devā cātumahārājikā, santi devā tāvatiṁsā, santi devā yāmā, santi devā tusitā, santi devā nimmānaratino, santi devā paranimmitavasavattino, santi devā brahmakāyikā, santi devā tatuttari.
segs.e: ‘There are the gods of the four great kings, the gods of the thirty-three, the gods of Yama, the joyful gods, the gods who love to create, the gods who control what is created by others, the gods of the Divinity’s host, and gods even higher than these.

segs.p: Yathārūpāya saddhāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tatthupapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā saddhā saṁvijjati.
segs.e: When those deities passed away from here, they were reborn there because of their faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom. I, too, have the same kind of faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.’

segs.p: Yathārūpena sīlena samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tatthupapannā, mayhampi tathārūpaṁ sīlaṁ saṁvijjati.
Yathārūpena sutena samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tatthupapannā, mayhampi tathārūpaṁ sutaṁ saṁvijjati.
Yathārūpena cāgena samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tatthupapannā, mayhampi tathārūpo cāgo saṁvijjati.
Yathārūpāya paññāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tatthupapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā paññā saṁvijjatī’ti.

Tassa attano ca tāsañca devatānaṁ saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti, seyyathāpi, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa jātarūpassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: As they recollect the faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom of both themselves and those deities, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up. It’s just like cleansing corrupt native gold by exertion.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa jātarūpassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is corrupt native gold cleansed by applying effort?

segs.p: Ukkañca paṭicca, loṇañca paṭicca, gerukañca paṭicca, nāḷikasaṇḍāsañca paṭicca, purisassa ca tajjaṁ vāyāmaṁ paṭicca.
segs.e: With a furnace, flux, a blowpipe, and tongs, and by applying the appropriate effort.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa jātarūpassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how corrupt native gold is cleansed by exertion.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: In the same way, a corrupt mind is cleaned by applying effort.

segs.p: Kathañca, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti?
segs.e: And how is a corrupt mind cleaned by exertion?
It’s when a noble disciple recollects the deities:

segs.p: ‘santi devā cātumahārājikā, santi devā tāvatiṁsā …pe… santi devā tatuttari.
segs.e: ‘There are the gods of the four great kings, the gods of the thirty-three, the gods of Yama, the joyful gods, the gods who love to imagine, the gods who control what is imagined by others, the gods of the Divinity’s host, and gods even higher than these.

segs.p: Yathārūpāya saddhāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tatthupapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā saddhā saṁvijjati.
segs.e: When those deities passed away from here, they were reborn there because of their faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom. I, too, have the same kind of faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.’

segs.p: paññāya samannāgatā tā devatā ito cutā tatthupapannā, mayhampi tathārūpā paññā saṁvijjatī’ti.
Tassa attano ca tāsañca devatānaṁ saddhañca sīlañca sutañca cāgañca paññañca anussarato cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti.
segs.e: As they recollect the faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom of both themselves and those deities, their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, visākhe, ‘ariyasāvako devatuposathaṁ upavasati, devatāhi saddhiṁ saṁvasati, devatā ārabbha cittaṁ pasīdati, pāmojjaṁ uppajjati, ye cittassa upakkilesā te pahīyanti’.
segs.e: This is called: ‘A noble disciple who observes the sabbath of the deities, living together with the deities. And because they think of the deities their mind becomes clear, joy arises, and mental corruptions are given up.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, visākhe, upakkiliṭṭhassa cittassa upakkamena pariyodapanā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a corrupt mind is cleaned by applying effort.

segs.p: Sa kho so, visākhe, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Then that noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘yāvajīvaṁ arahanto pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā nihitadaṇḍā nihitasatthā lajjī dayāpannā sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharanti;
segs.e: ‘As long as they live, the perfected ones give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. They are scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ pāṇātipātaṁ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharāmi.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up killing living creatures, renouncing the rod and the sword. I’ll be scrupulous and kind, and live full of sympathy for all living beings.

segs.p: Imināpi aṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissati.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.

segs.p: Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭiviratā dinnādāyī dinnapāṭikaṅkhī, athenena sucibhūtena attanā viharanti;
segs.e: As long as they live, the perfected ones give up stealing. They take only what’s given, and expect only what’s given. They keep themselves clean by not thieving.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ adinnādānaṁ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato dinnādāyī dinnapāṭikaṅkhī, athenena sucibhūtena attanā viharāmi.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up stealing. I’ll take only what’s given, and expect only what’s given. I’ll keep myself clean by not thieving.

segs.p: Imināpi aṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissati.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.

segs.p: Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto abrahmacariyaṁ pahāya brahmacārī ārācārī viratā methunā gāmadhammā;
segs.e: As long as they live, the perfected ones give up unchastity. They are chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ abrahmacariyaṁ pahāya brahmacārī ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up unchastity. I will be chaste, set apart, refraining from the vulgar act of sex.

segs.p: Imināpi aṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissati.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.

segs.p: Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭiviratā saccavādī saccasandhā thetā paccayikā avisaṁvādakā lokassa;
segs.e: As long as they live, the perfected ones give up lying. They speak the truth and stick to the truth. They’re honest and dependable, and don’t trick the world with their words.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ musāvādaṁ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato saccavādī saccasandho theto paccayiko avisaṁvādako lokassa.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up lying. I’ll speak the truth and stick to the truth. I’ll be honest and dependable, and won’t trick the world with my words.

segs.p: Imināpi aṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissati.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.

segs.p: Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ pahāya surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā;
segs.e: As long as they live, the perfected ones give up intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānaṁ pahāya surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.

segs.p: Imināpi aṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissati.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.

segs.p: Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto ekabhattikā rattūparatā viratā vikālabhojanā;
segs.e: As long as they live, the perfected ones eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night and from food at the wrong time.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ ekabhattiko rattūparato virato vikālabhojanā.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will eat in one part of the day, abstaining from eating at night and food at the wrong time.

segs.p: Imināpi aṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissati.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.
As long as they live, the perfected ones refrain from seeing shows of dancing, singing, and music; and attiring and adorning themselves with garlands, fragrance, and makeup.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ naccagītavāditavisūkadassanamālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇamaṇḍanavibhūsanaṭṭhānā paṭivirato.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will refrain from seeing shows of dancing, singing, and music; and attiring and adorning myself with garlands, fragrance, and makeup.

segs.p: Imināpi aṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissati.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.

segs.p: Yāvajīvaṁ arahanto uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭiviratā nīcaseyyaṁ kappenti mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā;
segs.e: As long as they live, the perfected ones give up high and luxurious beds. They sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: ahampajja imañca rattiṁ imañca divasaṁ uccāsayanamahāsayanaṁ pahāya uccāsayanamahāsayanā paṭivirato nīcaseyyaṁ kappemi mañcake vā tiṇasanthārake vā.
segs.e: I, too, for this day and night will give up high and luxurious beds. I’ll sleep in a low place, either a cot or a grass mat.

segs.p: Imināpi aṅgena arahataṁ anukaromi, uposatho ca me upavuttho bhavissatī’ti.
segs.e: I will observe the sabbath by doing as the perfected ones do in this respect.’
That’s the sabbath of the noble ones.

segs.p: Evaṁ upavuttho kho, visākhe, ariyuposatho mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṁso mahājutiko mahāvipphāro.
segs.e: When the sabbath of the noble ones is observed like this it’s very fruitful and beneficial and brilliant and bountiful.
How much so?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, visākhe, yo imesaṁ soḷasannaṁ mahājanapadānaṁ pahūtarattaratanānaṁ issariyādhipaccaṁ rajjaṁ kāreyya, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: Suppose you were to rule as sovereign lord over these sixteen great countries—Aṅga, Magadha, Kāsi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Cetī, Vaccha, Kuru, Pañcāla, Maccha, Sūrasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhāra, and Persia—full of the seven treasures.

segs.p: aṅgānaṁ, magadhānaṁ, kāsīnaṁ, kosalānaṁ, vajjīnaṁ, mallānaṁ, cetīnaṁ, vaṅgānaṁ, kurūnaṁ, pañcālānaṁ, macchānaṁ, sūrasenānaṁ, assakānaṁ, avantīnaṁ, gandhārānaṁ, kambojānaṁ, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgatassa uposathassa etaṁ kalaṁ nāgghati soḷasiṁ.
segs.e: This wouldn’t be worth a sixteenth part of the sabbath with its eight factors.
Why is that?

segs.p: Kapaṇaṁ, visākhe, mānusakaṁ rajjaṁ dibbaṁ sukhaṁ upanidhāya.
segs.e: Because human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.

segs.p: Yāni, visākhe, mānusakāni paññāsa vassāni, cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Fifty years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods of the four great kings.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni pañca vassasatāni cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of the four great kings is five hundred of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods of the four great kings.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yaṁ, visākhe, mānusakaṁ vassasataṁ, tāvatiṁsānaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: A hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods of the thirty-three.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbaṁ vassasahassaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of the thirty-three is a thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā tāvatiṁsānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods of the thirty-three.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yāni, visākhe, mānusakāni dve vassasatāni, yāmānaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Two hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods of Yama.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni dve vassasahassāni yāmānaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of Yama is two thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā yāmānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods of Yama.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yāni, visākhe, mānusakāni cattāri vassasatāni, tusitānaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Four hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the joyful gods.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni cattāri vassasahassāni tusitānaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the joyful gods is four thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā tusitānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the joyful gods.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yāni, visākhe, mānusakāni aṭṭha vassasatāni, nimmānaratīnaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Eight hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods who love to create.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni aṭṭha vassasahassāni nimmānaratīnaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods who love to create is eight thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā nimmānaratīnaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods who love to create.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’

segs.p: Yāni, visākhe, mānusakāni soḷasa vassasatāni, paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ eso eko rattindivo.
segs.e: Sixteen hundred years in the human realm is one day and night for the gods who control what is created by others.
Thirty such days make up a month.
Twelve such months make up a year.

segs.p: Tena saṁvaccharena dibbāni soḷasa vassasahassāni paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods who control what is created by others is sixteen thousand of these heavenly years.

segs.p: Ṭhānaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, vijjati yaṁ idhekacco itthī vā puriso vā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṁ uposathaṁ upavasitvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā paranimmitavasavattīnaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyya.
segs.e: It’s possible that some woman or man who has observed the eight-factored sabbath will—when their body breaks up, after death—be reborn in the company of the gods who control what is created by others.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho panetaṁ, visākhe, sandhāya bhāsitaṁ:
segs.e: This is what I was referring to when I said:
‘Human kingship is a poor thing compared to the happiness of the gods.’
You shouldn’t kill living creatures, or steal,

segs.p: Musā na bhāse na ca majjapo siyā;
segs.e: or lie, or drink liquor.
Be chaste, refraining from sex,
and don’t eat at night, the wrong time.

segs.p: Mālaṁ na dhāre na ca gandhamācare,
segs.e: Not wearing garlands or applying fragrance,
you should sleep on a low bed, <j>or a mat on the ground.
This is the eight-factored sabbath, they say,
revealed by the Buddha, <j>who has gone to suffering’s end.

segs.p: Cando ca suriyo ca ubho sudassanā,
segs.e: The moon and sun are both fair to see,
radiating as far as they revolve.
Those dispellers of darkness, travelers in midair,
shine in the firmament, dazzling the quarters.
All of the wealth that’s found in this realm—
pearls, gems, fine beryl too,
mountain gold or lustrous gold,
or the native gold called ‘coruscant’—
they’re not worth a sixteenth part
of the sabbath with its eight factors,
as starlight cannot rival the moon.

segs.p: Tasmā hi nārī ca naro ca sīlavā,
segs.e: So an ethical woman or man,
who has observed the eight-factored sabbath,
having made merit whose outcome is happiness,
blameless, they go to a heavenly place.”
Numbered Discourses 3.71
8. Ānanda
With Channa

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho channo paribbājako yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Channa went up to Venerable Ānanda and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho channo paribbājako āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to Ānanda:

segs.p: “tumhepi, āvuso ānanda, rāgassa pahānaṁ paññāpetha, dosassa pahānaṁ paññāpetha, mohassa pahānaṁ paññāpethā”ti.
segs.e: “Reverend Ānanda, do you advocate giving up greed, hate, and delusion?”

segs.p: “Mayaṁ kho, āvuso, rāgassa pahānaṁ paññāpema, dosassa pahānaṁ paññāpema, mohassa pahānaṁ paññapemā”ti.
segs.e: “We do, reverend.”

segs.p: “Kiṁ pana tumhe, āvuso, rāge ādīnavaṁ disvā rāgassa pahānaṁ paññāpetha, kiṁ dose ādīnavaṁ disvā dosassa pahānaṁ paññāpetha, kiṁ mohe ādīnavaṁ disvā mohassa pahānaṁ paññāpethā”ti?
segs.e: “But what drawbacks have you seen, Reverend Ānanda, that you advocate giving up greed, hate, and delusion?”

segs.p: “Ratto kho, āvuso, rāgena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti;
segs.e: “A greedy person, overcome by greed, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: rāge pahīne nevattabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na cetasikaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: When greed has been given up, they don’t intend to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They don’t experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Ratto kho, āvuso, rāgena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati;
segs.e: A greedy person does bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: rāge pahīne neva kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, na vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, na manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: When greed has been given up, they don’t do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Ratto kho, āvuso, rāgena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti;
segs.e: A greedy person doesn’t truly understand what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both.

segs.p: rāge pahīne attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: When greed has been given up, they truly understand what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both.

segs.p: Rāgo kho, āvuso, andhakaraṇo acakkhukaraṇo aññāṇakaraṇo paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṁvattaniko.
segs.e: Greed is a destroyer of sight, vision, and knowledge. It blocks wisdom, it’s on the side of distress, and it doesn’t lead to extinguishment.
A hateful person, overcome by hate, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. …

segs.p: mūḷho kho, āvuso, mohena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto attabyābādhāyapi ceteti, parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti;
segs.e: A deluded person, overcome by delusion, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: mohe pahīne nevattabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na parabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na ubhayabyābādhāyapi ceteti, na cetasikaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: When delusion has been given up, they don’t intend to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They don’t experience mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Mūḷho kho, āvuso, mohena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati;
segs.e: A deluded person does bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: mohe pahīne neva kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, na vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, na manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: When delusion has been given up, they don’t do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Mūḷho kho, āvuso, mohena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti;
segs.e: A deluded person doesn’t truly understand what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both.

segs.p: mohe pahīne attatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, paratthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti, ubhayatthampi yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: When delusion has been given up, they truly understand what’s for their own good, the good of another, or the good of both.

segs.p: Moho kho, āvuso, andhakaraṇo acakkhukaraṇo aññāṇakaraṇo paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṁvattaniko.
segs.e: Delusion is a destroyer of sight, vision, and knowledge; it blocks wisdom, it’s on the side of distress, and it doesn’t lead to extinguishment.

segs.p: Idaṁ kho mayaṁ, āvuso, rāge ādīnavaṁ disvā rāgassa pahānaṁ paññāpema.
segs.e: This is the drawback we’ve seen in greed, hate, and delusion, and this is why we advocate giving them up.”

segs.p: Idaṁ dose ādīnavaṁ disvā dosassa pahānaṁ paññāpema.
Idaṁ mohe ādīnavaṁ disvā mohassa pahānaṁ paññāpemā”ti.
“Atthi panāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti?
segs.e: “But, reverend, is there a path and a practice for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion?”

segs.p: “Atthāvuso, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti.
segs.e: “There is, reverend, a path and a practice for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion.”

segs.p: “Katamo panāvuso, maggo katamā paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti?
segs.e: “Well, what is it?”
“It is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso, maggo ayaṁ paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāyā”ti.
segs.e: This is the path, this is the practice for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion.”

segs.p: “Bhaddako kho, āvuso, maggo bhaddikā paṭipadā etassa rāgassa dosassa mohassa pahānāya.
segs.e: “This is a fine path, a fine practice, for giving up that greed, hate, and delusion.
Just this much is enough for diligence.”
Numbered Discourses 3.72
8. Ānanda
A Disciple of the Ājīvakas

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro ājīvakasāvako gahapati yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so ājīvakasāvako gahapati āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then a householder who was a disciple of the Ājīvaka ascetics went up to Venerable Ānanda, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to Ānanda:
“Honorable Ānanda, whose teaching is well explained?
Who in the world is practicing well?
Who in the world has done well?”

segs.p: “Tena hi, gahapati, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi, yathā te khameyya tathā naṁ byākareyyāsi.
segs.e: “Well then, householder, I’ll ask you about this in return, and you can answer as you like.
What do you think, householder?

segs.p: ye rāgassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desenti, dosassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desenti, mohassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desenti, tesaṁ dhammo svākkhāto no vā?
segs.e: Is the teaching of those who teach for giving up greed, hate, and delusion well explained or not?
Or how do you see this?”

segs.p: “Ye, bhante, rāgassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desenti, dosassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desenti, mohassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desenti, tesaṁ dhammo svākkhāto.
segs.e: “The teaching of those who teach for giving up greed, hate, and delusion is well explained.
That’s how I see it.”
“What do you think, householder?

segs.p: ye rāgassa pahānāya paṭipannā, dosassa pahānāya paṭipannā, mohassa pahānāya paṭipannā, te loke suppaṭipannā no vā?
segs.e: Are those who practice for giving up greed, hate, and delusion practicing well or not?
Or how do you see this?”

segs.p: “Ye, bhante, rāgassa pahānāya paṭipannā, dosassa pahānāya paṭipannā, mohassa pahānāya paṭipannā, te loke suppaṭipannā.
segs.e: “Those who practice for giving up greed, hate, and delusion are practicing well.
That’s how I see it.”
“What do you think, householder?

segs.p: yesaṁ rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo, yesaṁ doso pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo, yesaṁ moho pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo, te loke sukatā no vā?
segs.e: Have those who’ve given up greed, hate, and delusion—so they’re cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future—done well in the world, or not?
Or how do you see this?”

segs.p: “Yesaṁ, bhante, rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo, yesaṁ doso pahīno …pe… yesaṁ moho pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo, te loke sukatā.
segs.e: “Those who’ve given up greed, hate, and delusion have done well in the world.
That’s how I see it.”
“So, householder, you’ve declared:

segs.p: ‘ye, bhante, rāgassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desenti, dosassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desenti, mohassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desenti, tesaṁ dhammo svākkhāto’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching of those who teach for giving up greed, hate, and delusion is well explained.’
And you’ve declared:

segs.p: ‘ye, bhante, rāgassa pahānāya paṭipannā, dosassa pahānāya paṭipannā, mohassa pahānāya paṭipannā, te loke suppaṭipannā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Those who practice for giving up greed, hate, and delusion are practicing well.’
And you’ve declared:

segs.p: ‘yesaṁ, bhante, rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo, yesaṁ doso pahīno …pe… yesaṁ moho pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo, te loke sukatā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Those who’ve given up greed, hate, and delusion have done well in the world.’”
“It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Na ceva nāma sadhammukkaṁsanā bhavissati, na ca paradhammāpasādanā.
segs.e: There’s no acclaiming your own teaching or disrespecting someone else’s,

segs.p: Āyataneva dhammadesanā, attho ca vutto, attā ca anupanīto.
segs.e: just teaching what’s relevant in that context. The goal is spoken of, but the self is not involved.

segs.p: Tumhe, bhante ānanda, rāgassa pahānāya dhammaṁ desetha, dosassa …pe… mohassa pahanāya dhammaṁ desetha.
segs.e: You, sir, teach Dhamma for giving up greed, hate, and delusion.
Your teaching is well explained.

segs.p: Tumhe, bhante ānanda, rāgassa pahānāya paṭipannā, dosassa …pe… mohassa pahānāya paṭipannā.
segs.e: You, sir, practice for giving up greed, hate, and delusion.
You in the world are practicing well.

segs.p: Tumhākaṁ, bhante ānanda, rāgo pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo, tumhākaṁ doso pahīno …pe… tumhākaṁ moho pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṅkato āyatiṁ anuppādadhammo.
segs.e: You’ve given up greed, hate, and delusion.
You in the world have done well.
Excellent, sir! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ ayyena ānandena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, Master Ānanda has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bhante ānanda, taṁ bhagavantaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the Buddha, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ ayyo ānando dhāretu, ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may Master Ānanda remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 3.73
8. Ānanda
With Mahānāma the Sakyan
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā gilānā vuṭṭhito hoti aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā.
segs.e: Now at that time the Buddha had recently recovered from an illness.

segs.p: Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “dīgharattāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā evaṁ dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi:
segs.e: “For a long time, sir, I have understood your teaching like this:
‘Knowledge is for those with immersion, not those without immersion.’

segs.p: Samādhi nu kho, bhante, pubbe, pacchā ñāṇaṁ;
segs.e: But, sir, does immersion come first, then knowledge?
Or does knowledge come first, then immersion?”
Then Venerable Ānanda thought,
“The Buddha has recently recovered from an illness,

segs.p: Ayañca mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṁ atigambhīraṁ pañhaṁ pucchati.
segs.e: and this Mahānāma asks him a question that’s too deep.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ ekamantaṁ apanetvā dhammaṁ deseyyan”ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I take him off to one side and teach him the Dhamma?”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ bāhāyaṁ gahetvā ekamantaṁ apanetvā mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Ānanda took Mahānāma by the arm, led him off to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “sekhampi kho, mahānāma, sīlaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā, asekhampi sīlaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā; sekhopi samādhi vutto bhagavatā, asekhopi samādhi vutto bhagavatā; sekhāpi paññā vuttā bhagavatā, asekhāpi paññā vuttā bhagavatā.
segs.e: “Mahānāma, the Buddha has spoken of the ethics, immersion, and wisdom of a trainee; and the ethics, immersion, and wisdom of an adept.
What is the ethics of a trainee?

segs.p: Idha, mahānāma, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.
This is called the ethics of a trainee.
And what is the immersion of a trainee?

segs.p: Idha, mahānāma, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.
This is called the immersion of a trainee.
And what is the wisdom of a trainee?

segs.p: Idha, mahānāma, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: They truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.
This is called the wisdom of a trainee.

segs.p: Sa kho so, mahānāma, ariyasāvako evaṁ sīlasampanno evaṁ samādhisampanno evaṁ paññāsampanno āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Then a noble disciple—accomplished in ethics, immersion, and wisdom—realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, mahānāma, sekhampi sīlaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā, asekhampi sīlaṁ vuttaṁ bhagavatā; sekhopi samādhi vutto bhagavatā, asekhopi samādhi vutto bhagavatā; sekhāpi paññā vuttā bhagavatā, asekhāpi paññā vuttā bhagavatā”ti.
segs.e: In this way the Buddha has spoken of the ethics, immersion, and wisdom of both a trainee and an adept.”
Numbered Discourses 3.74
8. Ānanda
Jains

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho abhayo ca licchavi paṇḍitakumārako ca licchavi yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho abhayo licchavi āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Licchavis Abhaya and Paṇḍitakumāra went up to Venerable Ānanda, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “nigaṇṭho, bhante, nāṭaputto sabbaññū sabbadassāvī aparisesaṁ ñāṇadassanaṁ paṭijānāti:
segs.e: “Sir, the Jain ascetic of the Ñātika clan claims to be all-knowing and all-seeing, to know and see everything without exception, thus:

segs.p: ‘carato ca me tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṁ samitaṁ ñāṇadassanaṁ paccupaṭṭhitan’ti.
segs.e: ‘Knowledge and vision are constantly and continually present to me, while walking, standing, sleeping, and waking.’

segs.p: So purāṇānaṁ kammānaṁ tapasā byantībhāvaṁ paññāpeti navānaṁ kammānaṁ akaraṇā setughātaṁ.
segs.e: He advocates the elimination of past deeds by fervent mortification, and breaking the bridge by not doing any new deeds.

segs.p: Iti kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo, dukkhakkhayā vedanākkhayo, vedanākkhayā sabbaṁ dukkhaṁ nijjiṇṇaṁ bhavissati—
segs.e: So with the ending of deeds, suffering ends; with the ending of suffering, feeling ends; and with the ending of feeling, all suffering will have been worn away.

segs.p: evametissā sandiṭṭhikāya nijjarāya visuddhiyā samatikkamo hoti.
segs.e: This is how to go beyond suffering by means of this purification by wearing away in the present life.
What, sir, does the Buddha say about this?”

segs.p: “Tisso kho imā, abhaya, nijjarā visuddhiyo tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātā sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: “Abhaya, these three kinds of purification by wearing away have been rightly explained by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha. They are in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, abhaya, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s when, Abhaya, a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: So navañca kammaṁ na karoti, purāṇañca kammaṁ phussa phussa byantīkaroti.
segs.e: They don’t perform any new deeds, and old deeds are eliminated by experiencing their results little by little.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhīti.
segs.e: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Sa kho so, abhaya, bhikkhu evaṁ sīlasampanno vivicceva kāmehi …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Then a mendicant accomplished in ethics, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.

segs.p: So navañca kammaṁ na karoti, purāṇañca kammaṁ phussa phussa byantīkaroti.
segs.e: They don’t perform any new deeds, and old deeds are eliminated by experiencing their results little by little.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhīti.
segs.e: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Sa kho so, abhaya, bhikkhu evaṁ samādhisampanno āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Then a mendicant accomplished in immersion realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: So navañca kammaṁ na karoti, purāṇañca kammaṁ phussa phussa byantīkaroti.
segs.e: They don’t perform any new deeds, and old deeds are eliminated by experiencing their results little by little.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhīti.
segs.e: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Imā kho, abhaya, tisso nijjarā visuddhiyo tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātā sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three kinds of purification by wearing away that have been rightly explained by the Buddha … in order to realize extinguishment.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, paṇḍitakumārako licchavi abhayaṁ licchaviṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Paṇḍitakumāra said to Abhaya,

segs.p: “kiṁ pana tvaṁ, samma abhaya, āyasmato ānandassa subhāsitaṁ subhāsitato nābbhanumodasī”ti?
segs.e: “Dear Abhaya, is there anything in what Ānanda has said so well that you would disagree with?”

segs.p: “Kyāhaṁ, samma paṇḍitakumāraka, āyasmato ānandassa subhāsitaṁ subhāsitato nābbhanumodissāmi.
segs.e: “How could I not agree with what was said so well by Ānanda?

segs.p: Muddhāpi tassa vipateyya yo āyasmato ānandassa subhāsitaṁ subhāsitato nābbhanumodeyyā”ti.
segs.e: If anyone didn’t agree with him, their head would explode!”
Numbered Discourses 3.75
8. Ānanda
Support

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Ye, ānanda, anukampeyyātha ye ca sotabbaṁ maññeyyuṁ mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā te vo, ānanda, tīsu ṭhānesu samādapetabbā nivesetabbā patiṭṭhāpetabbā.
segs.e: “Ānanda, those who you have sympathy for, and those worth listening to—friends and colleagues, relatives and family—should be encouraged, supported, and established in three things.
What three?
Experiential confidence in the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ, buddho bhagavā’ti,
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’
Experiential confidence in the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti,
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’
Experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’
There might be change in the four principal states—

segs.p: pathavīdhātuyā āpodhātuyā tejodhātuyā vāyodhātuyā, na tveva buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa siyā aññathattaṁ tatridaṁ aññathattaṁ.
segs.e: earth, water, air, and fire—but a noble disciple with experiential confidence in the Buddha would never change.

segs.p: So vatānanda, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato ariyasāvako nirayaṁ vā tiracchānayoniṁ vā pettivisayaṁ vā upapajjissatīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: In this context, ‘change’ means that such a noble disciple will be reborn in hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm: this is quite impossible.
There might be change in the four principal states—

segs.p: pathavīdhātuyā āpodhātuyā tejodhātuyā vāyodhātuyā, na tveva dhamme …pe…
segs.e: earth, water, air, and fire—but a noble disciple with experiential confidence in the teaching …

segs.p: na tveva saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa siyā aññathattaṁ tatridaṁ aññathattaṁ.
segs.e: or the Saṅgha would never change.

segs.p: So vatānanda, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato ariyasāvako nirayaṁ vā tiracchānayoniṁ vā pettivisayaṁ vā upapajjissatīti netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
segs.e: In this context, ‘change’ means that such a noble disciple will be reborn in hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm: this is quite impossible.

segs.p: Ye, ānanda, anukampeyyātha ye ca sotabbaṁ maññeyyuṁ mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā te vo, ānanda, imesu tīsu ṭhānesu samādapetabbā nivesetabbā patiṭṭhāpetabbā”ti.
segs.e: Those who you have sympathy for, and those worth listening to—friends and colleagues, relatives and family—should be encouraged, supported, and established by you in these three things.”
Numbered Discourses 3.76
8. Ānanda
Continued Existence (1st)

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, they speak of this thing called ‘continued existence’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhavo hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is continued existence defined?”

segs.p: “Kāmadhātuvepakkañca, ānanda, kammaṁ nābhavissa, api nu kho kāmabhavo paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: “If, Ānanda, there were no deeds to result in the sensual realm, would continued existence in the sensual realm still come about?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Iti kho, ānanda, kammaṁ khettaṁ, viññāṇaṁ bījaṁ, taṇhā sneho.
segs.e: “So, Ānanda, deeds are the field, consciousness is the seed, and craving is the moisture.

segs.p: Avijjānīvaraṇānaṁ sattānaṁ taṇhāsaṁyojanānaṁ hīnāya dhātuyā viññāṇaṁ patiṭṭhitaṁ evaṁ āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti hoti. (…)
segs.e: The consciousness of sentient beings—shrouded by ignorance and fettered by craving—is established in a lower realm. That’s how there is regeneration into a new state of existence in the future.

segs.p: Rūpadhātuvepakkañca, ānanda, kammaṁ nābhavissa, api nu kho rūpabhavo paññāyethā”ti?
segs.e: If there were no deeds to result in the realm of luminous form, would continued existence in the realm of luminous form still come about?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Iti kho, ānanda, kammaṁ khettaṁ, viññāṇaṁ bījaṁ, taṇhā sneho.
segs.e: “So, Ānanda, deeds are the field, consciousness is the seed, and craving is the moisture.

segs.p: Avijjānīvaraṇānaṁ sattānaṁ taṇhāsaṁyojanānaṁ majjhimāya dhātuyā viññāṇaṁ patiṭṭhitaṁ evaṁ āyatiṁ punabbhavābhinibbatti hoti. (…)
