segs.e: Some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm because of accomplishment in ethics, mind, or view.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, apaṇṇako maṇi uddhaṁ khitto yena yeneva patiṭṭhāti suppatiṭṭhitaṁyeva patiṭṭhāti;
segs.e: It’s like throwing sure-bet dice: they always fall the right side up.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, sīlasampadāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti, cittasampadāhetu vā sattā …pe… diṭṭhisampadāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjanti.
segs.e: In the same way, some sentient beings, when their body breaks up, after death, are reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm because of accomplishment in ethics, mind, or view.
These are the three accomplishments.”
Numbered Discourses 3.119
12. Bound for Loss
Action
“Mendicants, there are three failures.
What three?
Failure in action, livelihood, and view.
And what is failure in action?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti …pe… samphappalāpī hoti.
segs.e: It’s when someone kills living creatures, steals, commits sexual misconduct, and uses speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.
This is called ‘failure in action’.
And what is failure in livelihood?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchāājīvo hoti, micchāājīvena jīvikaṁ kappeti.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has wrong livelihood and earns a living by wrong livelihood.
This is called ‘failure in livelihood’.
And what is failure in view?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchādiṭṭhiko hoti viparītadassano:
segs.e: It’s when someone has wrong view, a distorted perspective, such as:

segs.p: ‘natthi dinnaṁ, natthi yiṭṭhaṁ …pe… ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘There’s no meaning in giving, sacrifice, or offerings. There’s no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There’s no afterlife. There’s no such thing as mother and father, or beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there’s no ascetic or brahmin who is rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describes the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’
This is called ‘failure in view’.
These are the three failures.
There are three accomplishments.
What three?
Accomplishment in action, livelihood, and view.
And what is accomplishment in action?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti …pe… samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when someone doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, or use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.
This is called ‘accomplishment in action’.
And what is accomplishment in livelihood?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammāājīvo hoti, sammāājīvena jīvikaṁ kappeti.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has right livelihood and earns a living by right livelihood.
This is called ‘accomplishment in livelihood’.
And what is accomplishment in view?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammādiṭṭhiko hoti aviparītadassano:
segs.e: It’s when someone has right view, an undistorted perspective, such as:

segs.p: ‘atthi dinnaṁ, atthi yiṭṭhaṁ …pe… ye imañca lokaṁ parañca lokaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti.
segs.e: ‘There is meaning in giving, sacrifice, and offerings. There are fruits and results of good and bad deeds. There is an afterlife. There are such things as mother and father, and beings that are reborn spontaneously. And there are ascetics and brahmins who are rightly comported and rightly practiced, and who describe the afterlife after realizing it with their own insight.’
This is called ‘accomplishment in view’.
These are the three accomplishments.”
Numbered Discourses 3.120
12. Bound for Loss
Purity (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these three kinds of purity.
What three?
Purity of body, speech, and mind.
And what is purity of body?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when someone doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, or commit sexual misconduct.
This is called ‘purity of body’.
And what is purity of speech?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when someone doesn’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.
This is called ‘purity of speech’.
And what is purity of mind?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco anabhijjhālu hoti abyāpannacitto sammādiṭṭhiko.
segs.e: It’s when someone is content, kind-hearted, and has right view.
This is called ‘purity of mind’.
These are the three kinds of purity.”
Numbered Discourses 3.121
12. Bound for Loss
Purity (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are these three kinds of purity.
What three?
Purity of body, speech, and mind.
And what is purity of body?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, abrahmacariyā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, or have sex.
This is called ‘purity of body’.
And what is purity of speech?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.
This is called ‘purity of speech’.
And what is purity of mind?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ kāmacchandaṁ: ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ kāmacchando’ti pajānāti; asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ kāmacchandaṁ: ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ kāmacchando’ti pajānāti; yathā ca anuppannassa kāmacchandassa uppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca uppannassa kāmacchandassa pahānaṁ hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca pahīnassa kāmacchandassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant who has sensual desire in them understands ‘I have sensual desire in me.’ When they don’t have sensual desire in them, they understand ‘I don’t have sensual desire in me.’ They understand how sensual desire arises; how, when it’s already arisen, it’s given up; and how, once it’s given up, it doesn’t arise again in the future.

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ byāpādaṁ: ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ byāpādo’ti pajānāti; asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ byāpādaṁ: ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ byāpādo’ti pajānāti; yathā ca anuppannassa byāpādassa uppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca uppannassa byāpādassa pahānaṁ hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca pahīnassa byāpādassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti;
segs.e: When they have ill will in them they understand ‘I have ill will in me’; and when they don’t have ill will in them they understand ‘I don’t have ill will in me’. They understand how ill will arises; how, when it’s already arisen, it’s given up; and how, once it’s given up, it doesn’t arise again in the future.

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ thinamiddhaṁ: ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ thinamiddhan’ti pajānāti; asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ thinamiddhaṁ: ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ thinamiddhan’ti pajānāti; yathā ca anuppannassa thinamiddhassa uppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca uppannassa thinamiddhassa pahānaṁ hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca pahīnassa thinamiddhassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti;
segs.e: When they have dullness and drowsiness in them they understand ‘I have dullness and drowsiness in me’; and when they don’t have dullness and drowsiness in them they understand ‘I don’t have dullness and drowsiness in me’. They understand how dullness and drowsiness arise; how, when they’ve already arisen, they’re given up; and how, once they’re given up, they don’t arise again in the future.

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ uddhaccakukkuccaṁ: ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ uddhaccakukkuccan’ti pajānāti; asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ uddhaccakukkuccaṁ: ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ uddhaccakukkuccan’ti pajānāti; yathā ca anuppannassa uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca uppannassa uddhaccakukkuccassa pahānaṁ hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca pahīnassa uddhaccakukkuccassa āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti;
segs.e: When they have restlessness and remorse in them they understand ‘I have restlessness and remorse in me’; and when they don’t have restlessness and remorse in them they understand ‘I don’t have restlessness and remorse in me’. They understand how restlessness and remorse arise; how, when they’ve already arisen, they’re given up; and how, once they’re given up, they don’t arise again in the future.

segs.p: santaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ vicikicchaṁ: ‘atthi me ajjhattaṁ vicikicchā’ti pajānāti; asantaṁ vā ajjhattaṁ vicikicchaṁ: ‘natthi me ajjhattaṁ vicikicchā’ti pajānāti; yathā ca anuppannāya vicikicchāya uppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca uppannāya vicikicchāya pahānaṁ hoti, tañca pajānāti; yathā ca pahīnāya vicikicchāya āyatiṁ anuppādo hoti, tañca pajānāti.
segs.e: When they have doubt in them they understand ‘I have doubt in me’; and when they don’t have doubt in them they understand ‘I don’t have doubt in me’. They understand how doubt arises; how, when it’s already arisen, it’s given up; and how, once it’s given up, it doesn’t arise again in the future.
This is called ‘purity of mind’.
These are the three kinds of purity.
Purity of body, purity of speech,
and undefiled purity of heart.
A pure one, blessed with purity,
has washed off all bad things, they say.”
Numbered Discourses 3.122
12. Bound for Loss
Sagacity
“Mendicants, there are these three kinds of sagacity.
What three?
Sagacity of body, speech, and mind.
And what is sagacity of body?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, abrahmacariyā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, or have sex.
This is called ‘sagacity of body’.
And what is sagacity of speech?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.
This is called ‘sagacity of speech’.
And what is sagacity of mind?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.
This is called ‘sagacity of mind’.
These are the three kinds of sagacity.
A sage in body, a sage in speech,
a sage undefiled in heart;
a sage, blessed with sagacity,
has given up everything, they say.”
Numbered Discourses 3.123
13. Kusinārā
At Kusinārā

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kusinārāyaṁ viharati baliharaṇe vanasaṇḍe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kusinārā in the Forest of Offerings.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā upanissāya viharati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, take the case of a mendicant living supported by a town or village.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā upasaṅkamitvā svātanāya bhattena nimanteti.
segs.e: A householder or their child approaches and invites them for the next day’s meal.
The mendicant accepts if they want.

segs.p: So tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena tassa gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamati; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdati.
segs.e: When the night has passed, they robe up in the morning, take their bowl and robe, and approach that householder’s home, where they sit on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ so gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeti sampavāreti.
segs.e: The householder or their child serves and satisfies them with their own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.
The mendicant thinks:

segs.p: ‘sādhu vata myāyaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeti sampavāretī’ti.
segs.e: ‘It’s so good that this householder serves me with delicious fresh and cooked foods.’
Then they think:

segs.p: ‘aho vata māyaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā āyatimpi evarūpena paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeyya sampavāreyyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘I really hope this householder serves me with delicious fresh and cooked foods in the future, too.’

segs.p: So taṁ piṇḍapātaṁ gathito mucchito ajjhosanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
segs.e: They eat that food tied, infatuated, attached, blind to the drawbacks, and not understanding the escape.

segs.p: So tattha kāmavitakkampi vitakketi, byāpādavitakkampi vitakketi, vihiṁsāvitakkampi vitakketi.
segs.e: They think about it with sensual, malicious, or cruel thoughts.

segs.p: Evarūpassāhaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno dinnaṁ na mahapphalanti vadāmi.
segs.e: A gift to such a mendicant is not very fruitful, I say.
Why is that?
Because that mendicant is negligent.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā upanissāya viharati.
segs.e: Take another case of a mendicant living supported by a town or village.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā upasaṅkamitvā svātanāya bhattena nimanteti.
segs.e: A householder or their child approaches and invites them for the next day’s meal.
The mendicant accepts if they want.

segs.p: So tassā rattiyā accayena pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena tassa gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamati; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdati.
segs.e: When the night has passed, they robe up in the morning, take their bowl and robe, and approach that householder’s home, where they sit on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Tamenaṁ so gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeti sampavāreti.
segs.e: The householder or their child serves and satisfies them with their own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.
It never occurs to them:

segs.p: ‘sādhu vata myāyaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeti sampavāretī’ti.
segs.e: ‘It’s so good that the householder or their child serves and satisfies me with their own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.’
They don’t think:

segs.p: ‘aho vata māyaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā āyatimpi evarūpena paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappeyya sampavāreyyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘I really hope this householder serves me with delicious fresh and cooked foods in the future, too.’

segs.p: So taṁ piṇḍapātaṁ agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.
segs.e: They eat that almsfood untied, uninfatuated, unattached, seeing the drawback, and understanding the escape.

segs.p: So tattha nekkhammavitakkampi vitakketi, abyāpādavitakkampi vitakketi, avihiṁsāvitakkampi vitakketi.
segs.e: They think about it with thoughts of renunciation, good will, or harmlessness.

segs.p: Evarūpassāhaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno dinnaṁ mahapphalanti vadāmi.
segs.e: A gift to such a mendicant is very fruitful, I say.
Why is that?
Because that mendicant is diligent.”
Numbered Discourses 3.124
13. At Kusinārā
Arguments

segs.p: “Yassaṁ, bhikkhave, disāyaṁ bhikkhū bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṁ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti, manasi kātumpi me esā, bhikkhave, disā na phāsu hoti, pageva gantuṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I’m not even comfortable thinking about a place where mendicants fight—quarreling and disputing, continually wounding each other with barbed words—let alone going there.
I come to a conclusion about them:

segs.p: ‘addhā te āyasmanto tayo dhamme pajahiṁsu, tayo dhamme bahulamakaṁsu.
segs.e: ‘Clearly those venerables have given up three things and cultivated three things.’
What three things have they given up?
Thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.
What three things have they cultivated?
Sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts. …

segs.p: Yassaṁ, bhikkhave, disāyaṁ bhikkhū bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṁ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti, manasi kātumpi me esā, bhikkhave, disā na phāsu hoti, pageva gantuṁ.

segs.e: I come to a conclusion about them:

segs.p: ‘addhā te āyasmanto ime tayo dhamme pajahiṁsu, ime tayo dhamme bahulamakaṁsu’.
segs.e: ‘Clearly those venerables have given up three things and cultivated three things.’

segs.p: Yassaṁ pana, bhikkhave, disāyaṁ bhikkhū samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṁ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharanti, gantumpi me esā, bhikkhave, disā phāsu hoti, pageva manasi kātuṁ.
segs.e: I feel comfortable going to a place where the mendicants live in harmony—appreciating each other, without quarreling, blending like milk and water, and regarding each other with kindly eyes—let alone thinking about it.
I come to a conclusion about them:

segs.p: ‘addhā te āyasmanto tayo dhamme pajahiṁsu, tayo dhamme bahulamakaṁsu.
segs.e: ‘Clearly those venerables have given up three things and cultivated three things.’
What three things have they given up?
Sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts.
What three things have they cultivated?
Thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness. …

segs.p: Yassaṁ, bhikkhave, disāyaṁ bhikkhū samaggā sammodamānā avivadamānā khīrodakībhūtā aññamaññaṁ piyacakkhūhi sampassantā viharanti, gantumpi me esā, bhikkhave, disā phāsu hoti, pageva manasi kātuṁ.

segs.e: I come to a conclusion about them:

segs.p: ‘addhā te āyasmanto ime tayo dhamme pajahiṁsu, ime tayo dhamme bahulamakaṁsū’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Clearly those venerables have given up three things and cultivated three things.’”
Numbered Discourses 3.125
13. At Kusinārā
The Gotamaka Shrine

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati gotamake cetiye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Gotamaka Shrine.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, I teach based on direct knowledge, not without direct knowledge.

segs.p: Sanidānāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desemi, no anidānaṁ.
segs.e: I teach with reasons, not without them.

segs.p: Sappāṭihāriyāhaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammaṁ desemi, no appāṭihāriyaṁ.
segs.e: I teach with a demonstrable basis, not without it.

segs.p: Tassa mayhaṁ, bhikkhave, abhiññāya dhammaṁ desayato no anabhiññāya, sanidānaṁ dhammaṁ desayato no anidānaṁ, sappāṭihāriyaṁ dhammaṁ desayato no appāṭihāriyaṁ, karaṇīyo ovādo, karaṇīyā anusāsanī.
segs.e: Since this is so, you should follow my advice and instruction.

segs.p: Alañca pana vo, bhikkhave, tuṭṭhiyā, alaṁ attamanatāya, alaṁ somanassāya:
segs.e: This is enough for you to feel joyful, delighted, and happy:
‘The Blessed One is a fully awakened Buddha! The teaching is well explained! The Saṅgha is practicing well!’”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
segs.e: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṁ bhaññamāne sahassī lokadhātu akampitthāti.
segs.e: And while this discourse was being spoken, the thousandfold galaxy shook.
Numbered Discourses 3.126
13. Kusinārā
Bharaṇḍu Kālāma

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṁ caramāno yena kapilavatthu tadavasari.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans when he arrived at Kapilavatthu.

segs.p: Assosi kho mahānāmo sakko: “bhagavā kira kapilavatthuṁ anuppatto”ti.
segs.e: Mahānāma the Sakyan heard that he had arrived.

segs.p: Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: He went up to the Buddha, bowed, and stood to one side. The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “Gaccha, mahānāma, kapilavatthusmiṁ, tathārūpaṁ āvasathaṁ jāna yatthajja mayaṁ ekarattiṁ vihareyyāmā”ti.
segs.e: “Go into Kapilavatthu, Mahānāma, and check if there’s a suitable guest house where I can spend the night.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavato paṭissutvā kapilavatthuṁ pavisitvā kevalakappaṁ kapilavatthuṁ anvāhiṇḍanto nāddasa kapilavatthusmiṁ tathārūpaṁ āvasathaṁ yatthajja bhagavā ekarattiṁ vihareyya.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Mahānāma. He returned to Kapilavatthu and searched all over the city, but he couldn’t see a suitable guest house for the Buddha to spend the night.

segs.p: Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahānāma went up to the Buddha, and said to him,

segs.p: “natthi, bhante, kapilavatthusmiṁ tathārūpo āvasatho yatthajja bhagavā ekarattiṁ vihareyya.
segs.e: “Sir, there’s no suitable guest house in Kapilavatthu for you to spend the night.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhante, bharaṇḍu kālāmo bhagavato purāṇasabrahmacārī.
segs.e: But there is this Bharaṇḍu the Kālāma, who used to be the Buddha’s spiritual companion.
Why don’t you spend the night at his hermitage?”
“Go, Mahānāma, and set out a mat.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavato paṭissutvā yena bharaṇḍussa kālāmassa assamo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā santharaṁ paññāpetvā udakaṁ ṭhapetvā pādānaṁ dhovanāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Mahānāma. He went to Bharaṇḍu’s hermitage, where he set out a mat, and got foot-washing water ready. Then he went back to the Buddha and said to him,

segs.p: “santhato, bhante, santhāro, udakaṁ ṭhapitaṁ pādānaṁ dhovanāya.
segs.e: “The mat and foot-washing water are set out.
Please, sir, go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā yena bharaṇḍussa kālāmassa assamo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha went to Bharaṇḍu’s hermitage, sat down on the seat spread out,
and washed his feet.
Then it occurred to Mahānāma,
“It’s too late to pay homage to the Buddha today.
He’s tired.

segs.p: Sve dānāhaṁ bhagavantaṁ payirupāsissāmī”ti bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Tomorrow I’ll pay homage to the Buddha.” He bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho mahānāmo sakko tassā rattiyā accayena yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then, when the night had passed, Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “tayo khome, mahānāma, satthāro santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Mahānāma, there are these three teachers found in the world.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, mahānāma, ekacco satthā kāmānaṁ pariññaṁ paññāpeti;
segs.e: One teacher advocates the complete understanding of sensual pleasures,

segs.p: na rūpānaṁ pariññaṁ paññāpeti, na vedanānaṁ pariññaṁ paññāpeti.
segs.e: but not of forms or feelings.

segs.p: Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco satthā kāmānaṁ pariññaṁ paññāpeti, rūpānaṁ pariññaṁ paññāpeti;
segs.e: One teacher advocates the complete understanding of sensual pleasures and forms,
but not of feelings.

segs.p: Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco satthā kāmānaṁ pariññaṁ paññāpeti, rūpānaṁ pariññaṁ paññāpeti, vedanānaṁ pariññaṁ paññāpeti.
segs.e: One teacher advocates the complete understanding of sensual pleasures, forms, and feelings.

segs.p: Ime kho, mahānāma, tayo satthāro santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the three teachers found in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ, mahānāma, tiṇṇaṁ satthārānaṁ ekā niṭṭhā udāhu puthu niṭṭhā”ti?
segs.e: Do these three teachers have the same end or different ends?”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bharaṇḍu kālāmo mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Bharaṇḍu said to Mahānāma,
“Say they’re the same, Mahānāma!”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, bhagavā mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said,
“Say they’re different, Mahānāma!”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho bharaṇḍu kālāmo mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a second time, Bharaṇḍu said,
“Say they’re the same, Mahānāma!”

segs.p: Dutiyampi kho bhagavā mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said,
“Say they’re different, Mahānāma!”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho bharaṇḍu kālāmo mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: For a third time, Bharaṇḍu said,
“Say they’re the same, Mahānāma!”

segs.p: Tatiyampi kho bhagavā mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said,
“Say they’re different, Mahānāma!”
Then it occurred to Bharaṇḍu,

segs.p: “mahesakkhassa vatamhi mahānāmassa sakkassa sammukhā samaṇena gotamena yāvatatiyaṁ apasādito.
segs.e: “The Buddha has rebuked me three times in front of this illustrious Mahānāma.
Why don’t I leave Kapilavatthu?”

segs.p: Atha kho bharaṇḍu kālāmo kapilavatthumhā pakkāmi.
segs.e: Then Bharaṇḍu the Kālāma left Kapilavatthu,

segs.p: Yaṁ kapilavatthumhā pakkāmi tathā pakkantova ahosi na puna paccāgacchīti.
segs.e: never to return.
Numbered Discourses 3.127
13. Kusinārā
With Hatthaka

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho hatthako devaputto abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṁ jetavanaṁ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā:
segs.e: Then, late at night, the glorious godling Hatthaka, lighting up the entire Jeta’s Grove, went up to the Buddha. Thinking,

segs.p: “bhagavato purato ṭhassāmī”ti osīdatimeva saṁsīdatimeva, na sakkoti saṇṭhātuṁ.
segs.e: “I will stand before the Buddha,” he sank and melted down, and wasn’t able to stay still.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi nāma sappi vā telaṁ vā vālukāya āsittaṁ osīdatimeva saṁsīdatimeva, na saṇṭhāti;
segs.e: It’s like when ghee or oil is poured on sand, it sinks and melts down, and can’t remain stable.

segs.p: “bhagavato purato ṭhassāmī”ti osīdatimeva saṁsīdatimeva, na sakkoti saṇṭhātuṁ.
Atha kho bhagavā hatthakaṁ devaputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Hatthaka,
“Hatthaka, manifest a solid incarnation.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti, kho hatthako devaputto bhagavato paṭissutvā oḷārikaṁ attabhāvaṁ abhinimminitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” replied Hatthaka. He manifested a solid incarnation, bowed to the Buddha, and stood to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ ṭhitaṁ kho hatthakaṁ devaputtaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “Ye te, hatthaka, dhammā pubbe manussabhūtassa pavattino ahesuṁ, api nu te te dhammā etarahi pavattino”ti?
segs.e: “Hatthaka, I wonder whether you still promulgate now the teachings that you promulgated when you were a human being?”

segs.p: “Ye ca me, bhante, dhammā pubbe manussabhūtassa pavattino ahesuṁ, te ca me dhammā etarahi pavattino;
segs.e: “I still promulgate the teachings that I promulgated as a human being.

segs.p: ye ca me, bhante, dhammā pubbe manussabhūtassa nappavattino ahesuṁ, te ca me dhammā etarahi pavattino.
segs.e: And I also promulgate teachings that I didn’t promulgate as a human being.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhante, bhagavā etarahi ākiṇṇo viharati bhikkhūhi bhikkhunīhi upāsakehi upāsikāhi rājūhi rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi;
segs.e: Just as the Buddha these days lives crowded by monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen; by rulers and their chief ministers, and monastics of other religions and their disciples,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, ākiṇṇo viharāmi devaputtehi.
segs.e: so I live crowded by the godlings.

segs.p: Dūratopi, bhante, devaputtā āgacchanti hatthakassa devaputtassa santike ‘dhammaṁ sossāmā’ti.
segs.e: The godlings come from far away, thinking, ‘We’ll hear the teaching in the presence of Hatthaka.’

segs.p: Tiṇṇāhaṁ, bhante, dhammānaṁ atitto appaṭivāno kālaṅkato.
segs.e: Sir, I passed away without getting enough of three things.
What three?

segs.p: Bhagavato ahaṁ, bhante, dassanassa atitto appaṭivāno kālaṅkato;
segs.e: Seeing the Buddha;
hearing the true teaching;

segs.p: saṅghassāhaṁ, bhante, upaṭṭhānassa atitto appaṭivāno kālaṅkato.
segs.e: and serving the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, tiṇṇaṁ dhammānaṁ atitto appaṭivāno kālaṅkatoti.
segs.e: I passed away without getting enough of these three things.
I could never get enough
of seeing the Buddha,
serving the Saṅgha,
or hearing the teaching.
Training in the higher ethics,
loving to hear the true teaching,
Hatthaka has gone to the Aviha realm
without getting enough of these three things.”
Numbered Discourses 3.128
13. Kusinārā
Bitter

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ viharati isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya bārāṇasiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, entered Varanasi for alms.

segs.p: Addasā kho bhagavā goyogapilakkhasmiṁ piṇḍāya caramāno aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ rittassādaṁ bāhirassādaṁ muṭṭhassatiṁ asampajānaṁ asamāhitaṁ vibbhantacittaṁ pākatindriyaṁ.
segs.e: While the Buddha was walking for alms near the cow-hitching place at the wavy leaf fig, he saw a disgruntled monk who was looking for pleasure in external things, unmindful, without situational awareness or immersion, with straying mind and undisciplined faculties.
The Buddha said to him,
“Monk, don’t be bitter.

segs.p: Taṁ vata, bhikkhu, kaṭuviyakataṁ attānaṁ āmagandhena avassutaṁ makkhikā nānupatissanti nānvāssavissantīti, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjatī”ti.
segs.e: If you’re bitter, festering with putrefaction, flies will, without a doubt, plague and infest you.”

segs.p: Atha kho so bhikkhu bhagavatā iminā ovādena ovadito saṁvegamāpādi.
segs.e: Hearing this advice of the Buddha, that monk was struck with a sense of urgency.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṁ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then, after the meal, on his return from almsround, the Buddha told the mendicants what had happened. …

segs.p: “Idhāhaṁ, bhikkhave, pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya bārāṇasiṁ piṇḍāya pāvisiṁ.
Addasaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhikkhave, goyogapilakkhasmiṁ piṇḍāya caramāno aññataraṁ bhikkhuṁ rittassādaṁ bāhirassādaṁ muṭṭhassatiṁ asampajānaṁ asamāhitaṁ vibbhantacittaṁ pākatindriyaṁ.
Taṁ vata bhikkhu kaṭuviyakataṁ attānaṁ āmagandhena avassutaṁ makkhikā nānupatissanti nānvāssavissantīti, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjatī’ti.
Atha kho, bhikkhave, so bhikkhu mayā iminā ovādena ovadito saṁvegamāpādī”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, one of the mendicants said to the Buddha:
“Sir, what is this ‘bitterness’?
What is ‘putrefaction’?
And what are the ‘flies’?”
“Desire is bitterness;
ill will is the putrefaction;
and bad, unskillful thoughts are the flies.

segs.p: Taṁ vata, bhikkhu, kaṭuviyakataṁ attānaṁ āmagandhena avassutaṁ makkhikā nānupatissanti nānvāssavissantīti, netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjatīti.
segs.e: If you’re bitter, festering with putrefaction, flies will, without a doubt, plague and infest you.
When your eyes and ears are unguarded,
and you’re not restrained in your sense faculties,
flies—those lustful thoughts—
will plague you.
A mendicant who’s bitter,
festering with putrefaction,
is far from being extinguished,
distress is their lot.
Whether in village or wilderness,
if they don’t find serenity in themselves,
the fool, the simpleton departs,
honored only by flies.
But those who have ethics,
lovers of wisdom and peace,
they, being peaceful, sleep at ease,
since they’ve got rid of the flies.”
Numbered Discourses 3.129
13. Kusinārā
With Anuruddha (1st)

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā anuruddho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Anuruddha went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “idhāhaṁ, bhante, dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena yebhuyyena passāmi mātugāmaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjamānaṁ.
segs.e: “Sometimes, sir, with my clairvoyance that is purified and superhuman, I see that females—when their body breaks up, after death—are mostly reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Katihi nu kho, bhante, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjatī”ti?
segs.e: How many qualities do ladies have so that they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell?”

segs.p: “Tīhi kho, anuruddha, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: “When ladies have three qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, anuruddha, mātugāmo pubbaṇhasamayaṁ maccheramalapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati, majjhanhikasamayaṁ issāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati, sāyanhasamayaṁ kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati.
segs.e: A lady lives at home with a heart full of the stain of stinginess in the morning, jealousy at midday, and sexual desire in the evening.

segs.p: Imehi kho, anuruddha, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjatī”ti.
segs.e: When ladies possess these three qualities, when their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.”
Numbered Discourses 3.130
13. Kusinārā
With Anuruddha (2nd)

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Anuruddha went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā anuruddho āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to him:

segs.p: “idhāhaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṁ lokaṁ olokemi.
segs.e: “Here’s the thing, Reverend Sāriputta. With clairvoyance that is purified and surpasses the human, I survey the thousandfold galaxy.

segs.p: Āraddhaṁ kho pana me vīriyaṁ asallīnaṁ, upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā, passaddho kāyo asāraddho, samāhitaṁ cittaṁ ekaggaṁ.
segs.e: My energy is roused up and unflagging, my mindfulness is established and lucid, my body is tranquil and undisturbed, and my mind is immersed and unified in samādhi.

segs.p: Atha ca pana me nānupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuccatī”ti.
segs.e: But my mind is not freed from the defilements by not grasping.”

segs.p: “Yaṁ kho te, āvuso anuruddha, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: “Well, Reverend Anuruddha, when you say:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena sahassaṁ lokaṁ volokemī’ti, idaṁ te mānasmiṁ.
segs.e: ‘With clairvoyance that is purified and surpasses the human, I survey the thousandfold galaxy,’ that’s your conceit.

segs.p: Yampi te, āvuso anuruddha, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: And when you say:

segs.p: ‘āraddhaṁ kho pana me vīriyaṁ asallīnaṁ, upaṭṭhitā sati asammuṭṭhā, passaddho kāyo asāraddho, samāhitaṁ cittaṁ ekaggan’ti, idaṁ te uddhaccasmiṁ.
segs.e: ‘My energy is roused up and unflagging, my mindfulness is established and lucid, my body is tranquil and undisturbed, and my mind is immersed in samādhi,’ that’s your restlessness.

segs.p: Yampi te, āvuso anuruddha, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: And when you say:

segs.p: ‘atha ca pana me nānupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuccatī’ti, idaṁ te kukkuccasmiṁ.
segs.e: ‘But my mind is not freed from the defilements by not grasping,’ that’s your remorse.

segs.p: Sādhu vatāyasmā anuruddho ime tayo dhamme pahāya, ime tayo dhamme amanasikaritvā amatāya dhātuyā cittaṁ upasaṁharatū”ti.
segs.e: It would be good to give up these three things. Ignore them and apply your mind to freedom from death.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho aparena samayena ime tayo dhamme pahāya, ime tayo dhamme amanasikaritvā amatāya dhātuyā cittaṁ upasaṁhari.
segs.e: After some time Anuruddha gave up these three things. Ignoring them, he applied his mind to freedom from death.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā anuruddho eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then Anuruddha, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā anuruddho arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Anuruddha became one of the perfected.
Numbered Discourses 3.131
13. Kusinārā
Under Cover
“Mendicants, three things are conveyed under cover, not in the open.
What three?

segs.p: Mātugāmo, bhikkhave, paṭicchanno āvahati, no vivaṭo;
segs.e: Ladies are conveyed for marriage with a veil, not unveiled.

segs.p: brāhmaṇānaṁ, bhikkhave, mantā paṭicchannā āvahanti, no vivaṭā;
segs.e: Hymns of the brahmins are conveyed under cover, not openly.

segs.p: micchādiṭṭhi, bhikkhave, paṭicchannā āvahati, no vivaṭā.
segs.e: Wrong view is conveyed under cover, not in the open.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi paṭicchannāni āvahanti, no vivaṭāni.
segs.e: These three things are conveyed under cover, not in the open.

segs.p: Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, vivaṭāni virocanti, no paṭicchannāni.
segs.e: Three things dazzle in the open, not under cover.
What three?

segs.p: Candamaṇḍalaṁ, bhikkhave, vivaṭaṁ virocati, no paṭicchannaṁ;
segs.e: The moon dazzles in the open, not under cover.

segs.p: sūriyamaṇḍalaṁ, bhikkhave, vivaṭaṁ virocati, no paṭicchannaṁ;
segs.e: The sun dazzles in the open, not under cover.

segs.p: tathāgatappavedito dhammavinayo, bhikkhave, vivaṭo virocati, no paṭicchanno.
segs.e: The teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One dazzle in the open, not under cover.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi vivaṭāni virocanti, no paṭicchannānī”ti.
segs.e: These three things dazzle in the open, not under cover.”
Numbered Discourses 3.132
13. Kusinārā
Etchings
“Mendicants, these three individuals are found in the world.
What three?

segs.p: Pāsāṇalekhūpamo puggalo, pathavilekhūpamo puggalo, udakalekhūpamo puggalo.
segs.e: An individual like a line drawn in stone, an individual like a line drawn in sand, and an individual like a line drawn in water.
And who is the individual like a line drawn in stone?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo abhiṇhaṁ kujjhati.
segs.e: It’s an individual who is often angry,

segs.p: So ca khvassa kodho dīgharattaṁ anuseti.
segs.e: and their anger lingers for a long time.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pāsāṇe lekhā na khippaṁ lujjati vātena vā udakena vā, ciraṭṭhitikā hoti;
segs.e: It’s like a line drawn in stone, which isn’t quickly worn away by wind and water, but lasts for a long time.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo abhiṇhaṁ kujjhati.
segs.e: In the same way, an individual is often angry,

segs.p: So ca khvassa kodho dīgharattaṁ anuseti.
segs.e: and their anger lingers for a long time.
This is called an individual like a line drawn in stone.
And who is the individual like a line drawn in sand?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo abhiṇhaṁ kujjhati.
segs.e: It’s an individual who is often angry,

segs.p: So ca khvassa kodho na dīgharattaṁ anuseti.
segs.e: but their anger doesn’t linger long.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pathaviyā lekhā khippaṁ lujjati vātena vā udakena vā, na ciraṭṭhitikā hoti;
segs.e: It’s like a line drawn in sand, which is quickly worn away by wind and water, and doesn’t last long.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo abhiṇhaṁ kujjhati.
segs.e: In the same way, an individual is often angry,

segs.p: So ca khvassa kodho na dīgharattaṁ anuseti.
segs.e: but their anger doesn’t linger long.
This is called an individual like a line drawn in sand.
And who is the individual like a line drawn in water?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo āgāḷhenapi vuccamāno pharusenapi vuccamāno amanāpenapi vuccamāno sandhiyatimeva saṁsandatimeva sammodatimeva.
segs.e: It’s an individual who, though spoken to by someone in a rough, harsh, and disagreeable manner, still stays in touch, interacts with, and greets them.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, udake lekhā khippaṁyeva paṭivigacchati, na ciraṭṭhitikā hoti;
segs.e: It’s like a line drawn in water, which vanishes right away, and doesn’t last long.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo āgāḷhenapi vuccamāno pharusenapi vuccamāno amanāpenapi vuccamāno sandhiyatimeva saṁsandatimeva sammodatimeva.
segs.e: In the same way, an individual, though spoken to by someone in a rough, harsh, and disagreeable manner, still stays in touch, interacts with, and greets them.
This is called an individual like a line drawn in water.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the three individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 3.133
14. A Warrior
A Warrior

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato yodhājīvo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhyaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a warrior with three factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned as a factor of kingship.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo dūre pātī ca hoti akkhaṇavedhī ca mahato ca kāyassa padāletā.
segs.e: He’s a long-distance shooter, a marksman, one who shatters large objects.

segs.p: Imehi, kho, bhikkhave, tīhi aṅgehi samannāgato yodhājīvo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhyaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A warrior with these three factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned as a factor of kingship.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tīhi aṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with three factors is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What three?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dūre pātī ca hoti akkhaṇavedhī ca mahato ca kāyassa padāletā.
segs.e: They’re a long-distance shooter, a marksman, and one who shatters large objects.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dūre pātī hoti?
segs.e: And how is a mendicant a long-distance shooter?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yaṁ kiñci rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ rūpaṁ: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly sees any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Yā kāci vedanā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā yā dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ vedanaṁ: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
segs.e: They truly see any kind of feeling at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all feeling—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Yā kāci saññā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā yā dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ saññaṁ: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
segs.e: They truly see any kind of perception at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all perception—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Ye keci saṅkhārā atītānāgatapaccuppannā ajjhattā vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā hīnā vā paṇītā vā ye dūre santike vā, sabbe saṅkhāre: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
segs.e: They truly see any kind of choices at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all choices—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ: ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
segs.e: They truly see any kind of consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dūre pātī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is a long-distance shooter.
And how is a mendicant a marksman?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti; ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkhaṇavedhī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is a marksman.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahato kāyassa padāletā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a mendicant shatter large objects?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahantaṁ avijjākkhandhaṁ padāleti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant shatters the great mass of ignorance.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahato kāyassa padāletā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant shatters large objects.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these three qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 3.134
14. A Warrior
Assemblies
“Mendicants, there are these three assemblies.
What three?

segs.p: Ukkācitavinītā parisā, paṭipucchāvinītā parisā, yāvatāvinītā parisā—
segs.e: An assembly educated in fancy talk, an assembly educated in questioning, and an assembly educated to the fullest extent.
These are the three assemblies.”
Numbered Discourses 3.135
14. A Warrior
A Friend
“Mendicants, you should associate with a friend who has three factors.
What three?

segs.p: Duddadaṁ dadāti, dukkaraṁ karoti, dukkhamaṁ khamati—
segs.e: They give what is hard to give, they do what is hard to do, and they endure what is hard to endure.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi aṅgehi samannāgato mitto sevitabbo”ti.
segs.e: You should associate with a friend who has these three factors.”
Numbered Discourses 3.136
14. A Warrior
Arising

segs.p: “Uppādā vā, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṁ anuppādā vā tathāgatānaṁ, ṭhitāva sā dhātu dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, whether Realized Ones arise or not, this law of nature persists, this regularity of natural principles, this surety of natural principles:
all conditions are impermanent.
A Realized One awakens to this and comprehends it,

segs.p: Abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā ācikkhati deseti paññāpeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti:
segs.e: then he explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and discloses it:
‘All conditions are impermanent.’

segs.p: Uppādā vā, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṁ anuppādā vā tathāgatānaṁ ṭhitāva sā dhātu dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā.
segs.e: Whether Realized Ones arise or not, this law of nature persists, this regularity of natural principles, this surety of natural principles:
all conditions are suffering.
A Realized One awakens to this and comprehends it,

segs.p: Abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā ācikkhati deseti paññāpeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti:
segs.e: then he explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and discloses it:
‘All conditions are suffering.’

segs.p: Uppādā vā, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṁ anuppādā vā tathāgatānaṁ ṭhitāva sā dhātu dhammaṭṭhitatā dhammaniyāmatā.
segs.e: Whether Realized Ones arise or not, this law of nature persists, this regularity of natural principles, this surety of natural principles:
all things are not-self.
A Realized One awakens to this and comprehends it,

segs.p: Abhisambujjhitvā abhisametvā ācikkhati deseti paññāpeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti:
segs.e: then he explains, teaches, asserts, establishes, clarifies, analyzes, and discloses it:
‘All things are not-self.’”
Numbered Discourses 3.137
14. A Warrior
A Hair Blanket

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yāni kānici tantāvutānaṁ vatthānaṁ, kesakambalo tesaṁ paṭikiṭṭho akkhāyati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a hair blanket is said to be the worst kind of woven cloth.

segs.p: Kesakambalo, bhikkhave, sīte sīto, uṇhe uṇho, dubbaṇṇo, duggandho, dukkhasamphasso.
segs.e: It’s cold in the cold, hot in the heat, ugly, smelly, and unpleasant to touch.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yāni kānici puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇavādānaṁ makkhalivādo tesaṁ paṭikiṭṭho akkhāyati.
segs.e: In the same way, the teaching of the bamboo-staffed ascetic is said to be the worst of all the doctrines of the various ascetics and brahmins.
The bamboo-staffed ascetic, that futile man, has this doctrine and view:
‘There is no power in deeds, action, or energy.’

segs.p: Yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṁ atītamaddhānaṁ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tepi bhagavanto kammavādā ceva ahesuṁ kiriyavādā ca vīriyavādā ca.
segs.e: Those who were perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas in the past also taught the efficacy of deeds, action, and energy.
But the bamboo-staffed ascetic opposes them by saying:
‘There is no power in deeds, action, or energy.’

segs.p: Yepi te, bhikkhave, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṁ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tepi bhagavanto kammavādā ceva bhavissanti kiriyavādā ca vīriyavādā ca.
segs.e: Those who will be perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas in the future will also teach the efficacy of deeds, action, and energy.
But the bamboo-staffed ascetic opposes them by saying:
‘There is no power in deeds, action, or energy.’

segs.p: Ahampi, bhikkhave, etarahi arahaṁ sammāsambuddho kammavādo ceva kiriyavādo ca vīriyavādo ca.
segs.e: I too, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha in the present, teach the efficacy of deeds, action, and energy.
But the bamboo-staffed ascetic opposes me by saying:
‘There is no power in deeds, action, or energy.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, nadīmukhe khippaṁ uḍḍeyya bahūnaṁ macchānaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya anayāya byasanāya;
segs.e: It’s like a trap set at the mouth of a river, which would bring harm, suffering, calamity, and disaster for many fish.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, makkhali moghapuriso manussakhippaṁ maññe loke uppanno bahūnaṁ sattānaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya anayāya byasanāyā”ti.
segs.e: In the same way that futile man the bamboo-staffed ascetic is a trap for humans, it seems to me. He has come into the world for the harm, suffering, calamity, and disaster of many beings.”
Numbered Discourses 3.138
14. A Warrior
Accomplishment
“Mendicants, there are three accomplishments.
What three?
Accomplishment in faith, ethics, and wisdom.
These are the three accomplishments.”
Numbered Discourses 3.139
14. A Warrior
Growth
“Mendicants, there are three kinds of growth.
What three?
Growth in faith, ethics, and wisdom.
These are the three kinds of growth.”
Numbered Discourses 3.140
14. A Warrior
A Wild Colt

segs.p: “Tayo ca, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅke desessāmi tayo ca purisakhaḷuṅke.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you about three wild colts and three wild people.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“What are the three wild colts?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco assakhaḷuṅko javasampanno hoti; na vaṇṇasampanno, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: One wild colt is fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco assakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca; na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: Another wild colt is fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco assakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: While another wild colt is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.
These are the three wild colts.
And what are the three wild people?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno hoti; na vaṇṇasampanno, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: One wild person is fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca; na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: Another wild person is fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: While another wild person is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno hoti; na vaṇṇasampanno na ārohapariṇāhasampanno?
segs.e: And how is a wild person fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.
This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho saṁsādeti, no vissajjeti.
segs.e: But when asked a question about the teaching or training, they falter without answering.
This is how they’re not beautiful, I say.
And they don’t receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.
This is how they’re not well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno hoti; na vaṇṇasampanno, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: This is how a wild person is fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca; na ārohapariṇāhasampanno?
segs.e: And how is a wild person fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.
This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeti, no saṁsādeti.
segs.e: When asked a question about the teaching or training, they answer without faltering.
This is how they’re beautiful, I say.
But they don’t receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.
This is how they’re not well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca; na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: This is how a wild person is fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca?
segs.e: And how is a wild person fast, beautiful, and well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.
This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeti, no saṁsādeti.
segs.e: When asked a question about the teaching or training, they answer without faltering.
This is how they’re beautiful, I say.
They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.
This is how they’re well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisakhaḷuṅko javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: This is how a wild person is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.
These are the three wild people.”
Numbered Discourses 3.141
14. A Warrior
Excellent Horses

segs.p: “Tayo ca, bhikkhave, assaparasse desessāmi tayo ca purisaparasse.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you the three excellent horses and the three excellent people.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“What are the three excellent horses?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco assaparasso javasampanno hoti; na vaṇṇasampanno na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: One excellent horse is fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco assaparasso javasampanno hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca; na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: Another excellent horse is fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco assaparasso javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: While another excellent horse is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.
These are the three excellent horses.
What are the three excellent people?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco purisaparasso javasampanno hoti; na vaṇṇasampanno na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: One excellent person is fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco purisaparasso javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca; na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: Another excellent person is fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco purisaparasso javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: While another excellent person is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisaparasso javasampanno hoti; na vaṇṇasampanno, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno?
segs.e: And how is an excellent person fast, but not beautiful or well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, with the ending of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously. They’re extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.
This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho saṁsādeti, no vissajjeti.
segs.e: But when asked a question about the teaching or training, they falter without answering.
This is how they’re not beautiful, I say.
And they don’t receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Idamassa na ārohapariṇāhasmiṁ vadāmi. Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisaparasso javasampanno hoti;
segs.e: This is how they’re not well proportioned, I say. This is how an excellent person is fast,
but not beautiful or well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisaparasso javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno?
segs.e: And how is an excellent person fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, with the ending of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously. They’re extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.
This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeti, no saṁsādeti.
segs.e: When asked a question about the teaching or training, they answer without faltering.
This is how they’re beautiful, I say.
But they don’t receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.
This is how they’re not well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisaparasso javasampanno ca hoti; vaṇṇasampanno ca, na ārohapariṇāhasampanno.
segs.e: This is how an excellent person is fast and beautiful, but not well proportioned.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, purisaparasso javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca?
segs.e: And how is an excellent person fast, beautiful, and well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, with the ending of the five lower fetters, is reborn spontaneously. They’re extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.
This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeti, no saṁsādeti.
segs.e: When asked a question about the teaching or training, they answer without faltering.
This is how they’re beautiful, I say.
They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.
This is how they’re well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, purisaparasso javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: This is how an excellent person is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.
These are the three excellent people.”
Numbered Discourses 3.142
14. A Warrior
The Thoroughbred

segs.p: “Tayo ca, bhikkhave, bhadre assājānīye desessāmi tayo ca bhadre purisājānīye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you the three fine thoroughbred horses, and the three fine thoroughbred people.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“What are the three fine thoroughbred horses?
One fine thoroughbred horse …

segs.p: javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo bhadrā assājānīyā.
segs.e: These are the three fine thoroughbred horses.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, tayo bhadrā purisājānīyā?
segs.e: And what are the three fine thoroughbred people?
One fine thoroughbred person …

segs.p: javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.
And how is a fine thoroughbred person …

segs.p: javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca?
segs.e: fast, beautiful, and well proportioned?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.
This is how they’re fast, I say.

segs.p: Abhidhamme kho pana abhivinaye pañhaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeti, no saṁsādeti.
segs.e: When asked a question about the teaching or training, they answer without faltering.
This is how they’re beautiful, I say.
They receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.
This is how they’re well proportioned, I say.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhadro purisājānīyo javasampanno ca hoti vaṇṇasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: This is how a fine thoroughbred person is fast, beautiful, and well proportioned.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo bhadrā purisājānīyā”ti.
segs.e: These are the three fine thoroughbred people.”
Numbered Discourses 3.143
14. A Warrior
At the Peacocks’ Feeding Ground (1st)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati moranivāpe paribbājakārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, at the monastery for the wanderers in the peacocks’ feeding ground.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu accantaniṭṭho hoti accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosāno seṭṭho devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a mendicant with three qualities has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate sanctuary from the yoke, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal. They are best among gods and humans.
What three?

segs.p: Asekkhena sīlakkhandhena, asekkhena samādhikkhandhena, asekkhena paññākkhandhena.
segs.e: The entire spectrum of an adept’s ethics, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu accantaniṭṭho hoti accantayogakkhemī accantabrahmacārī accantapariyosāno seṭṭho devamanussānan”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these three qualities has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate sanctuary from the yoke, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal. They are best among gods and humans.”

segs.p: “Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bālo abyatto asappuriso khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo ca viññūnaṁ, bahuñca apuññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: “When a foolish, incompetent untrue person has three qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and reproved by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.
What three?

segs.p: Akusalena kāyakammena, akusalena vacīkammena, akusalena manokammena—
segs.e: Unskillful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind. …

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, tīhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo abyatto asappuriso khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo ca viññūnaṁ, bahuñca apuññaṁ pasavati.
Tīhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito viyatto sappuriso akkhataṁ anupahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, anavajjo ca hoti ananuvajjo ca viññūnaṁ, bahuñca puññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: When an astute, competent true person has three qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.

segs.p: Kusalena kāyakammena, kusalena vacīkammena, kusalena manokammena …pe….
segs.e: Skillful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind. …”
